Standing. The country does not yet have specific data protection legislation, the same speaker said. The government's national report to the Universal Periodic Review, published on 18 February 2025, lists a personal data protection bill among several awaiting discussion in the National People's Assembly.

Regulations. The bill leaves the organisation of the body it would create to a decree.

Application. Data protection matters are handled by several institutions, sector by sector.

Last twelve months. At an ECOWAS Court conference in Dakar on 22 September 2026, the professor said the bill provides for what it calls a "Data Protection Agency", and that its membership puts its independence at risk.

Not held. No law is enacted, and where the bill stands is not known: nothing shows it has moved since it was reported as awaiting discussion in 2025. Nothing is held on regulations or on any decision.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea has had a personal data protection law since 2016; whether it has been applied, or its supervisory body created, is not known.
GNQ.summary:
Authority. Articles 15 and 29 of the law name the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body, with a Secretaría Técnica and a Registro General under it. The law states that the body is to be created by a decree that will fix its structure.

Standing. Ley Núm. 1/2016, de Protección de Datos Personales, was sanctioned and promulgated by the President on 22 July 2016. It sets rules for the processing of personal data in the public and private sectors, and enters into force twenty days after its publication in the Boletín Oficial del Estado.

Regulations. The law leaves the structure of the Órgano Rector to a decree.

Application. The law places the power to sanction with the Minister of Telecommunications and New Technologies.

Last twelve months. The law in force is the one dated 22 July 2016.

Not held. Whether the decree creating the Órgano Rector was issued, whether any regulation was made under the law, and whether any decision or sanction has been taken under it. Nothing dated after 22 July 2016 is held.

KEN.short: Kenya's 2019 Data Protection Act is in force and its commissioner has fined businesses; the number of decisions in any one year is not known.
KEN.summary:
Authority. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was established under the Data Protection Act, 2019, and its first commissioner has been in office since 2020. In March 2025 it had offices in Nairobi, Kisumu, Mombasa, Eldoret, Machakos, Nyeri and Nakuru.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2019 is in force. The ICT Cabinet Secretary told the Senate in May 2026 that the Act is being enforced, and the office has issued fines under it since 2022.

Regulations. The Data Protection (Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors) Regulations, 2021 are in force under the Act. They set 24-month registration certificates and make processing on an expired certificate an offence.

Application. As at September 2024 the office had fined at least nine businesses a total of KES 26,275,000. Its bulletin states that by March 2025 it had issued 215 determinations and imposed penalties on 10 entities.

Last twelve months. In August 2026 the office published a draft guidance note on transfers of personal data to offshore AI providers. On 28 August 2026 it gave holders of expired registration certificates until 11 September 2026 to renew or face enforcement.

Not held. No count of decisions or sanctions for a single stated year: the figures to March 2025 are cumulative. The date the Act commenced is not given.

LBR.short: Liberia approved a data protection act in March 2026; it has no recorded decision, and whether the Commissioner has begun acting is not known.
LBR.summary:
Authority. The Act confers data protection functions on the Independent Information Commissioner, the oversight body created by the Freedom of Information Act of 2010.

Standing. The Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act of 2024 was approved on 9 March 2026 and printed on 23 March 2026. It takes effect on publication into handbills, and existing businesses have one year from the effective date to comply. President Boakai's promulgation of the law was announced on 19 August 2026.

Regulations. The Act requires implementing rules within 24 months of its taking effect.

Application. The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection said on 13 September 2026 that it is aware of its responsibilities under the Act, and that it took part in validating the legal framework.

Last twelve months. The House of Representatives had referred the President's bill to committee on 10 June 2025. The Act was approved on 9 March 2026, and its signing was reported on 20 August 2026.

Not held. Any regulation issued under the Act, and any decision, sanction or count of decisions under it. Whether the Independent Information Commissioner has begun acting under the Act is not held.

LBY.short: Whether Libya has a general data protection law, or one in preparation, is not known, so no stage is set.
LBY.summary: Not held. Whether Libya has a general data protection law, enacted or in preparation, and whether a supervisory authority exists. No regulation, decision or event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 is recorded.

LSO.short: Lesotho has a Data Protection Act of 2011 with no commission appointed; whether it has ever been applied or has regulations is not known.
LSO.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection Act has a Data Protection Commission under it. Cenfri, in an article published on 23 March 2026, says the Commission has remained unappointed.

Standing. Lesotho's general law is the Data Protection Act, which Cenfri dates to 2011. Cenfri says, in the article it published on 23 March 2026, that the Act has been law for over a decade.

Regulations. The nearest dated position is Cenfri's, published on 23 March 2026: the Data Protection Act has been law for over a decade.

Application. The nearest dated position concerns the body under the Act: Cenfri says, in its article of 23 March 2026, that the Data Protection Commission has remained unappointed.

Last twelve months. The latest dated position is Cenfri's article of 23 March 2026, which says that the Act has been law for over a decade and that its Commission has remained unappointed.

Not held. No regulation made under the Act and no decision applying it is held, nor is any event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026. The source that says the Commission is unappointed gives no date for that position beyond its own publication on 23 March 2026.

MAR.short: Morocco's 2009 data protection law is in force and its authority issues guidance; whether any controller has been sanctioned is not known.
MAR.summary:
Authority. The Commission nationale de contrôle de la protection des données à caractère personnel (CNDP) was installed in 2010 and acts under Law 09-08. Its president, Omar Seghrouchni, said on 4 August 2026 that it is strengthening an alert system that can go as far as sanctions.

Standing. Law 09-08 on personal data is in force: the CNDP cited ten of its articles to political parties in August 2026, and its president spoke that month of a law more than fifteen years in force.

Regulations. The CNDP validated five deliberations on 28 November 2025 setting model declaration and authorisation forms for cookies, newsletters, patient follow-up, healthcare video surveillance and workplace access control.

Application. The CNDP published a national register of notified processing operations in January 2023. On 28 August 2026 it issued guidance to political parties and voters for the legislative elections of 23 September 2026 and opened an information line, 3020. It runs a programme with public and private controllers that it calls Data-Tika.

Last twelve months. A proposed recast of Law 09-08, prepared with the Justice Ministry, has been sent to the Secrétariat général du gouvernement, the CNDP president said on 4 August 2026. A draft framework law on AI, data governance and digital identity, called Digital X.0, was under review by the same secretariat in November 2025. The CNDP signed a cooperation memorandum with Portugal's data protection authority on 8 February 2026.

Not held. No decision on a named controller and no published count of decisions, sanctions or complaints is held. No regulation under Law 09-08 is held, and what a 2023 amendment to the law changed is not known.

MDG.short: Madagascar has a data protection law of 2015 and an authority seated in 2025; whether the law has been applied is not known.
MDG.summary:
Authority. Article 28 of the law institutes the Commission Malagasy de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CMIL) as an independent authority of nine members named by decree in the Council of Ministers. Seven members were sworn in at the Cour suprême on 4 August 2025, and the commission elected a president and two vice-presidents on 14 August 2025.

Standing. Loi n° 2014-038 on the protection of personal data was adopted by the Assemblée nationale on 16 December 2014 and promulgated on 9 January 2015. The commission's procedures manual, approved in October 2025, takes the law as its legal basis.

Regulations. Décret n°2023-1541 of 6 December 2023 sets the commission's attributions, organisation and operation and governs the processing of personal data; Décret n°2025-696 of 18 June 2025 amended it. The commission's report of January 2026 cites a significant delay in adopting the law's application decrees.

Application. The commission reported in January 2026 that no processing declaration had been registered, that citizens' complaints had gone untreated for ten years and that it had neither premises nor staff. Its manual sets procedures for declarations, authorisations, audits, complaints and administrative sanctions, with a decision on a complaint due within 30 working days.

Last twelve months. The commission approved its first procedures manual on 17 October 2025, published on 3 December 2025. It joined the AFAPDP on 24 November 2025 and obtained a budget line of Ariary 2,411,579,000 in the 2026 Finance Law.

Not held. No decision, sanction or count of cases under the law. The date the law came into force is not stated.

MLI.short: Mali has a 2013 data protection law, applied by its authority with fines and complaints handled in 2025; the law's commencement date is not known.
MLI.summary:
Authority. Article 20 of the law institutes the Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel (APDP) as an independent administrative authority of 15 members. It sat in ordinary session on 3 August 2026 with all commissioners present and runs regional offices in Kayes, Sikasso, Ségou and Mopti.

Standing. Law no. 2013-015 on the protection of personal data was adopted by the National Assembly on 9 May 2013 and promulgated on 21 May 2013. On 3 August 2026 the APDP's president cited the law, as amended, as the basis for the authority's sanctions.

Regulations. Decree no. 2024-0300/PT-RM of 14 May 2024, made under the law, sets the fees payable to the APDP for declarations, authorisations and certification, and exempts non-profit public services.

Application. For 2025 the APDP's annual report, as summarised by Sahel Tribune, counts fines totalling 22 million FCFA and 51 complaints received, of which 28 were handled and four referred to the cybercrime prosecutor. The fines include 5 million FCFA on a Bamako clinic for obstructing a check of its video surveillance and 5 million FCFA on Société Aminata Konaté SARL for refusing a verification mission.

Last twelve months. The APDP opened an extraordinary session on 6 October 2025 to review about 2,000 declaration files and opened a regional office at Ségou on 4 December 2025. Its session of 3 August 2026 had over 1,000 files to examine.

Not held. The date the law came into force is not held: its text states none. The APDP's 2025 annual report is held only through a press summary, and no figure is held for sanctions issued in 2026.

MOZ.short: Mozambique has no data protection law; a bill was still being prepared in August 2026, and when it goes to parliament is not known.
MOZ.summary:
Authority. No data protection authority exists. The Data Protection Office was not yet established in October 2025, and a June 2025 report found no data regulatory authority. The draft law reviewed in September 2025 gives the role to the existing Regulatory Authority for ICT.

Standing. Mozambique has a draft law and no law. The minister for communications and digital transformation said on 22 July 2026 that a personal data protection law was still in preparation, and the president of INTIC said on 25 August 2026 that the authorities were preparing to submit the draft to parliament.

Regulations. A June 2025 inception report says Mozambique has drafted a Data Protection Bill and has not enacted a comprehensive data protection law.

Application. A World Bank and African Development Bank diagnostic, with evidence to spring 2025, recommends that the government adopt a data protection law.

Last twelve months. In October 2025 the bill had not been approved by Cabinet or submitted to Parliament. On 5 December 2025 the president of INTIC said it would go to Cabinet by June 2026. A round table reported on 28 August 2026 discussed the proposed law.

Not held. Whether the bill had reached Cabinet or parliament by 30 September 2026. There is no law, so no regulations or decisions under one.

MRT.short: Mauritania's 2017 data protection law is applied by its authority through opinions and rules; whether any controller has been sanctioned is not known.
MRT.summary:
Authority. The Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APD) was created by article 64 of the law as an independent body attached to the Prime Minister, and decree 2022-13 of 18 February 2022 governs its composition and operation. It met on 30 June 2026 under its president, with its members and the Government Commissioner present.

Standing. Law 2017-020 on the protection of personal data was promulgated on 22 July 2017. The APD's 2023-2026 strategic plan places itself under the law's entry into force, and its deliberation 002/2026 of 24 March 2026 applies articles 7, 11, 27, 37 and 40.

Regulations. Deliberation 004/2025 of 14 July 2025 requires the APD's prior authorisation for transfers to countries not on its list and lists 105 countries as adequate. Deliberation 005/2025 of 30 July 2025 requires it for public and private controllers using cloud services abroad.

Application. On 24 March 2026 the APD gave a favourable opinion, conditional on its remarks, on the joint decision authorising the system Maaden Mauritanie calls Maadeni. On 19 November 2025 it examined complaints 004-2025, 006-2025 and 007-2025, one of them with a bank's reply.

Last twelve months. On 19 November 2025 the APD approved a control reference framework and empowered its sworn agents to take part in inspection missions. On 29 April 2026 it approved amendments to deliberations 004/2025 and 005/2025 and discussed complaints 008-2025 and 001-2026. Its 30 June 2026 session had authorisation requests and ministries' compliance answers on its agenda.

Not held. No source gives a sanction, order or decision on a named controller, or a published count of decisions for a stated year, and the outcomes of the APD's sessions are mostly not stated. The law's commencement date, whether Mauritania has ratified the Malabo Convention and whether the law is under revision are not held.

MUS.short: Mauritius has the Data Protection Act 2017, and its office reported complaints closed and transfers decided in 2024; figures for 2025 are not known.
MUS.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection Office has been operational since 16 February 2009 and enforces the Data Protection Act 2017. Drudeisha Madhub is the Data Protection Commissioner.

Standing. Mauritius adopted its current data protection regime in 2017, after a first law in 2004 that was partly implemented in 2009. The Office reports on its enforcement of the Data Protection Act 2017 during 2024.

Regulations. Controllers and processors register under the Data Protection (Fees) Regulations 2020. Registrations since 1 August 2020 reached 21,219 controllers and 1,157 processors by 31 December 2024.

Application. For January to December 2024 the Office reports 179 new complaints, 39 complaints closed, 105 personal data breaches notified, 112 cross-border transfers authorised and 12 rejected, and four compliance inspections. The Commissioner said in May 2026 that her office issues 3,000 enforcement actions a year, 99 per cent of them resolved without prosecution.

Last twelve months. The Minister made regulations on 17 June 2026 requiring every controller to designate a data protection officer, to come into operation on 1 January 2027. The Commissioner said in May 2026 that Mauritius is going for the EU adequacy assessment in 2026, and amendments to bring in administrative fines are being introduced. In July 2026 the ICT Minister spoke of forthcoming amendments to the Act.

Not held. No figures for 2025 are held. The draft bill to amend the Act for EU adequacy carries no date beyond 2024, and the 2026 regulations are not yet in operation.

MWI.short: Malawi's Data Protection Act of 2024 is in force and applied through guidance only; whether any decision or sanction has been made is not known.
MWI.summary:
Authority. Section 4 of the Act designates the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA) as the Data Protection Authority. MACRA issued guidance in that role in October 2025, and in March 2026 the Authority operated under the regulator, which was working to make it an independent institution.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 3 of 2024) was passed on 7 December 2023, assented to on 31 January 2024 and published on 2 February 2024. The Authority's guideline of October 2025 says the Act applied at once to foreign controllers and to Malawian controllers with over 10,000 data subjects, and to all others from 3 June 2026.

Regulations. MACRA drafted the Data Protection (Data Processors Engagement) Regulations, 2025 under section 52 of the Act, dated 6 October 2025. In July 2026 the draft regulations it put to consultation were still to be finalised.

Application. The Authority published a compliance guideline and checklist on 17 October 2025, with a registration requirement for controllers of significant importance, and breach notification guidelines on 22 October 2025, setting a 72-hour notice to the Authority and to data subjects.

Last twelve months. In October 2025 the Public Private Partnership Commission issued terms of reference for a consultancy to operationalise the Authority and draft regulations. In March 2026 the World Bank announced renewed technical assistance to MACRA for data protection. On 13 July 2026 MACRA consulted stakeholders in Blantyre on draft regulations carrying annual registration fees of K50,000 to K7 million by turnover.

Not held. No decision, sanction or published count of decisions under the Act is held, and no regulation in force. No commencement notice for the Act is held.

NAM.short: Namibia has a draft Data Protection Bill, still being finalised in July 2026, and no law to apply; when it reaches Parliament is not known.
NAM.summary:
Authority. The 2020 draft of the Data Protection Bill establishes a Data Protection Supervisory Authority of Namibia in section 25, and the revised draft dated 2022 provides in its long title for the same authority and its powers, duties and functions.

Standing. The Data Protection Bill is a draft. The ICT minister, Emma Theofelus, said on 13 July 2026 that Namibia was finalising it.

Regulations. The bill the Ministry of Information and Communication Technology published for comment in 2022 is a 59-page draft with its gazette notice number left blank.

Application. An opposition MP, Rodney Cloete, said in August 2026 that Namibia has no data protection statute, and so no legal definition of a data controller and no rules on cross-border transfers.

Last twelve months. In August 2025 the minister said the bill, about 12 years in preparation, would be tabled in Parliament in September 2025. In January 2026 she said it had been through consultation and drafting and was ready for resubmission to the Cabinet Committee on Legislation, and in July 2026 that it was being finalised.

Not held. No source states that the bill has been tabled in Parliament, passed or enacted. Nothing dated since the 2022 draft says the supervisory authority has been set up, and no regulations or decisions are held.

NER.short: Niger's 2022 data protection law is in force, with compliance files and inspections in 2025; whether any decision was made under it is not known.
NER.summary:
Authority. The law creates the Haute Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel (HAPDP), attached to the Presidency, with ten members named by decree. Its president said in July 2025 that he took office on 18 September 2024 and that the plenary deliberates on authorisations and sanctions. Africa Data Protection reported on 13 June 2026 that the government had abolished the HAPDP by decree and split its powers between the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior.

Standing. Law no. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 on personal data protection is the general law, held in the HAPDP's consolidated text of April 2026. It repealed laws 2017-28 and 2019-71.

Regulations. The law has been amended by Law 2023-31 of 4 July 2023 and by Ordinances 2024-16 of 26 April 2024 and 2024-29 of 24 June 2024.

Application. The HAPDP's president said in July 2025 that the authority had processed 139 compliance files since September 2024, covering declarations, video-surveillance declarations and processing and transfer authorisations, and had run four control missions on mobile operators in 2025.

Last twelve months. The abolition of the HAPDP and the transfer of its powers to two ministries was reported on 13 June 2026.

Not held. No regulation made under the law is held, and no decision, sanction or count of complaints settled under it. The date the law came into force and the date of the decree abolishing the HAPDP are not held.

NGA.short: Nigeria's Data Protection Act of 2023 is in force and applied through fines and court orders; the number of decisions since mid-2024 is not known.
NGA.summary:
Authority. The Nigeria Data Protection Commission supervises the Act, having replaced the Nigeria Data Protection Bureau in June 2023. National Commissioner Vincent Olatunji heads it, and it keeps a register of data processors of major importance.

Standing. President Tinubu signed the Nigeria Data Protection Act on 12 June 2023, and the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory applied it in a judgment of 29 July 2026. A Nigeria Data Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was before the National Assembly in July 2026.

Regulations. The minister's office names the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 as the operating framework under the Act for all tiers of government. The Commission's Guidance Notice on Registration designates data controllers and processors of major importance.

Application. The Commission fined Multichoice Nigeria N766,242,500 in July 2025. On 29 July 2026 the court ordered Stanbic IBTC Bank to pay two former customers N15 million and erase their data. A Commission order fining Meta $32.8 million was set aside when the Federal High Court adopted a settlement. By 11 June 2024 the Commission said sanctions on seven firms had brought in N400 million.

Last twelve months. The Federal High Court upheld the Commission's power to register controllers and processors of major importance, and on 28 July 2026 the Commission directed every unregistered one to register. It opened investigations into Temu in February 2026 and into Remita and Sterling Bank on 1 April 2026, and moved into a new Abuja headquarters on 14 September 2026.

Not held. No count of decisions or sanctions for any period ending after 11 June 2024. The date on which the Meta order was set aside, and how far the Amendment Bill has gone in the National Assembly.

RWA.short: Rwanda's 2021 Data Protection Act is in force and the authority registers and trains controllers; whether any sanction or decision has been made is unknown.
RWA.summary:
Authority. The National Cyber Security Authority acts as the supervisory authority for personal data protection and privacy under the Data Protection Act.

Standing. Rwanda's Data Protection Act was introduced on 15 October 2021. It is in force: its two-year grace period ended on 15 October 2023, the date from which controllers and processors are held to it.

Regulations. Under the Act the authority issues registration certificates to data controllers and processors.

Application. By January 2026 the authority had registered data controllers and processors, trained over 100 Data Protection Officers in the public sector and run sector workshops for pharmacists and local government entities, all over the previous four years.

Last twelve months. For Data Privacy Week, 26 to 30 January 2026, the authority adopted the theme "Compliance is Beyond Registration". It moved from the awareness phase of 2022 to 2024 to capacity building, and now expects controllers to prove that they comply.

Not held. No source says whether regulations under the Act have been issued or are pending. No dated sanction or decision under the Act is on record, and no count of decisions is published.

SDN.short: Sudan had a data and artificial intelligence bill in draft in August 2026, with no law yet to apply; the bill's content is not known.
SDN.summary:
Authority. The draft law that would carry data protection is being prepared by the Justice Ministry together with the digital transformation ministry.

Standing. A data and artificial intelligence bill is in draft. On 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers discussed it and directed further study before approval by the interim parliament, a joint sitting of the Sovereignty and Ministers councils. On 11 August 2026 the Justice Ministry's under-secretary named it the 2026 Law on Regulating Data and Artificial Intelligence, meant to provide the legislative framework, data protection included.

Regulations. The bill is one of several draft bills from the digital transformation ministry that the Council of Ministers discussed on 6 August 2026.

Application. The law is one of three draft laws the Justice Ministry said on 11 August 2026 it is preparing.

Last twelve months. Both steps fall in August 2026: the Council of Ministers' direction of further study on 6 August, and the Justice Ministry's statement that the draft is in preparation on 11 August.

Not held. What the bill provides, whether it has gone to the interim parliament, and any date for a vote or commencement. No supervisory authority acting under a data protection law, no regulations and no decisions are held.

SEN.short: Senegal's 2008 data protection law is in force and applied, with figures published for April to June 2026; whether regulations exist under it is unknown.
SEN.summary:
Authority. The Commission de Protection des Données Personnelles (CDP) is constituted: it held two plenary sessions and issued decisions in April to June 2026. The law set it up as an independent administrative authority, and its president, Ousmane Thiongane, signed a partnership convention with Benin's authority in Cotonou, reported on 17 April 2026.

Standing. Law no. 2008-12 on the protection of personal data was enacted on 25 January 2008 and has been in force since 2014. On 27 March 2026 an expert told APS it is the current law, and the CDP issued receipts, authorisations and a rejection under it in April to June 2026.

Regulations. A workshop reported in July 2026 worked to finalise a draft data protection law and its implementing decree.

Application. For April to June 2026 the CDP reported 195 files handled, 153 declaration receipts and 39 authorisations issued, one processing rejected, and eight complaints and one report received and handled. Its plenary served a formal notice on SOLID SA, operator of the Kay Voter platform, for unsolicited prospecting by SMS, reported on 20 April 2024.

Last twelve months. The CDP relaunched the updating of the law at a two-day workshop at Saly, reported in July 2026, with the ministry committed to finalising the draft law and decree. In March 2026 an expert said a bill was reported to be in the circuit and that the National Assembly must vote it.

Not held. Whether any regulation is in force under Law no. 2008-12 is not stated. How far the bill to replace the law has got is not stated either.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone has no data protection law, only a bill Cabinet approved in April 2026; whether it has reached Parliament is not known.
SLE.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill would establish a single independent authority responsible for both data protection and access to information, the first such body in the country.

Standing. The law is a bill. The Information Minister announced in November 2025 that the Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill, 2025 had concluded its final national validation. On 21 April 2026 he announced that Cabinet had authorised enactment of a new Data Protection and Right to Access Information Act and approved the repeal of the Right to Access Information Commission Act.

Regulations. On 21 April 2026 the Ministry of Information and Civic Education and the Attorney-General's office were still to finalise the Bill and table it in Parliament.

Application. In November 2025 the Bill had submission to Cabinet and then to Parliament still to come.

Last twelve months. The Bill moved from final national validation in November 2025 to Cabinet approval on 21 April 2026.

Not held. No law is enacted, and whether the Bill has been tabled in Parliament is not held. No regulations and no decisions are held, and no source says there are none.

SOM.short: Somalia's 2023 data protection law is in force and its authority opened registration in 2026; whether any decision or sanction followed is not known.
SOM.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection Authority was inaugurated on 24 February 2024. The Act sets it up as an independent agency under a General Manager, with a Board of up to nine members.

Standing. Law No. 005 of 2023, the Data Protection Act, was ratified by both chambers of parliament and signed by the President in March 2023. A notice from the Authority, reported on 2 June 2026, requires registration under Article 32 of every entity that collects, stores, processes or shares personal data in Somalia.

Regulations. A review published on 11 June 2024 says the Authority issued an Implementation Regulation, guidance and an Alternative Dispute Resolution Procedure under Article 41. The Council of Ministers approved the Regulatory Framework for the Public Data Protection Law by majority vote, reported on 8 January 2026.

Application. The Authority published guidelines for implementing the law at the beginning of February 2024. By 2 June 2026 it had begun accepting registration applications from controllers and processors, and said it will issue certificates only to those meeting the conditions.

Last twelve months. The Regulatory Framework was approved after the Ministry of Communications and Technology said it had cleared constitutional, legal and technical procedures, reported on 6 February 2026. The Authority opened registration of controllers and processors, reported on 2 June 2026.

Not held. No named and dated decision, sanction or order under the law, and no published count of decisions for a stated period. The date the 2023 Act came into force.

SSD.short: South Sudan has no data protection law; a 2025 bill was being reviewed in May 2026, and whether it has reached parliament is not known.
SSD.summary:
Authority. The draft bill, when passed, will establish a Data Protection Commission to safeguard the personal data of online users, Radio Tamazuj reported on 20 November 2025.

Standing. South Sudan has no data protection law: the World Bank's identity diagnostic, published on 1 May 2026, states that the country has no national data protection or privacy law. A bill is being drafted. Digital security experts finalised what Radio Tamazuj calls the first Data Protection Policy Bill in October 2025, with the National Communication Authority and civil society, and a post dated 5 May 2026 reports a two-day workshop of over 30 stakeholders to review and validate the Data Protection Bill, 2025 (Version 1.0).

Regulations. Koneta's Executive Director said in a release dated 17 October 2025 that existing ICT regulations are limited.

Application. The World Bank diagnostic states that South Sudan has no national data protection and privacy regime.

Last twelve months. Paradigm Initiative and Koneta Hub convened lawmakers, civil society organisations and officials in Juba to review the draft bill and seek a parliamentary commitment to table it, in a release dated 17 October 2025. The ICT minister, Ateny Wek Ateny, said in December 2025 that the government would introduce the bill in 2026, drafted jointly by the ministries of information and justice. The validation workshop was reported on 5 May 2026, with members of parliament, civil society, the UNMISS legal unit and the National Communication Authority taking part.

Not held. Any bill tabled in parliament or any law enacted. No regulation and no decision on a controller is held, and what has happened to the bill since May 2026 is not held.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe enacted a data protection law in 2016; no sanction or decision under it is recorded, and its regulations are not known.
STP.summary:
Authority. The Agência Nacional de Protecção de Dados Pessoais (ANPDP) is, in Téla Nón's words, the body that by law authorises and supervises all data processing; its president is José Manuel Costa Alegre. Portugal's data protection commission received an ANPDP delegation on 16 June 2025 and names the agency a founding member of the Lusophone Data Protection Network.

Standing. Lei n.º 03/2016, on the protection of personal data of natural persons, was published in Diário da República n.º 39 of 10 May 2016. An International Bar Association chapter published in 2024 names it as the primary instrument of a framework that applies to processing by controllers headquartered or established in the country.

Regulations. The law itself provides for fines and criminal sanctions, which the ANPDP imposes together with ancillary measures.

Application. On 14 April 2026 the ANPDP's president met the president of the National Assembly to plan the agency's oversight of personal data in the automatic electoral roll.

Last twelve months. On 1 June 2026 the ANPDP signed a cooperation memorandum with Macau's data protection office, which Macau executive orders had authorised by 27 May.

Not held. Whether any regulation has been made under Law 03/2016, the date it came into force, and any named sanction, decision or published count under it. Nothing dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 bears on the law itself.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has a Data Protection Act of 2022, applied through enforcement notices in 2024 and 2025; the number of decisions made is not known.
SWZ.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection Act designates the Eswatini Communications Commission as the Eswatini Data Protection Authority. In June 2026 the Authority had powers to investigate breaches, resolve complaints and impose sanctions, and took complaints by website, email and phone.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2022 (No. 5 of 2022) was assented to and gazetted on 4 March 2022. In June 2026 the Commission's acting chief executive said the Act binds public and private bodies, ministries included, and requires a breach to be notified to the Authority within 72 hours. The deadline for organisations to comply was 31 March 2026.

Regulations. Notice No. 1/2024, issued in February 2024, made registration mandatory from 1 March 2024 for controllers and processors handling the data of more than ten people. General Notice No. 4/2024 directed every data controller to appoint a data protection officer by 30 May 2024.

Application. The Authority lists enforcement notices under section 41 of the Act issued to MTN Eswatini and Liberty Life Swaziland Limited in June 2024 and to the Royal Science Technology Park in March 2025. In June 2026 it opened a formal investigation into the Ministry of Home Affairs over unblurred national identity documents posted online.

Last twelve months. By February 2026 the Authority had launched its 2026 awareness campaign, "Take Control of Your Data". In September 2026 it was setting up information desks in major towns, after its own survey found 55.2% of the public finding the Authority difficult to access.

Not held. No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled is published for a stated year, and the newest enforcement notice on record is from March 2025. The outcome of the investigation opened in June 2026 is not reported.

SYC.short: Seychelles' Data Protection Act 2023 is in force and its commission handled 14 cases in 2025; whether any ended in a decision is not known.
SYC.summary:
Authority. The Act names the Information Commission, established under the Access to Information Act, as the competent authority, with powers to investigate, audit, issue enforcement notices and impose administrative fines of up to SCR200,000. The Commission took on the mandate at the end of December 2023 and in 2025 had a Chief Information Commissioner, two Information Commissioners and a chief executive in post.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023) was assented to on 19 December 2023 and bears the operative date 22 December 2023; it repeals the former Data Protection Act. The Commission administered it during 2025.

Regulations. The Act itself gave controllers and processors already processing data 18 months from commencement, to 22 June 2025, to conform.

Application. The Commission received four data protection cases in 2024, mostly from the non-banking financial sector, and 14 in 2025: six on data transfers, five breaches, two refused deletion requests and one consultation. It handled the 2025 cases by guidance, assessment and corrective advice.

Last twelve months. In January 2026 the Commission advertised a Senior Data Protection Analyst post. The National Assembly lists the Commission's annual report for 2025 as published on 13 April 2026. In that report the Chief Commissioner states that the Act remains at risk of being largely unenforced because the one budgeted technical post is unfilled.

Not held. No decision or sanction on a named controller and no count of cases settled is held, only cases received and handled. Whether regulations have been made under the Act is not held.

TCD.short: Chad is drafting a Digital Code with data protection provisions, announced in December 2025; it is not applied, and its progress since is not known.
TCD.summary:
Authority. The digital law that Chad's government is preparing is to incorporate international standards on cybersecurity, data protection and internet governance, as Minister Boukar Michel announced on 9 December 2025.

Standing. Chad is drafting a Digital Code, which the country calls the Code du Numérique. The minister said on 9 December 2025 that authorities were finalising the law, and a report published on 16 March 2026 described the code as under development since December 2025.

Regulations. The code that would carry the data protection provisions was under development in the report published on 16 March 2026.

Application. The Digital Code is to incorporate international standards on data protection, according to the report published on 16 March 2026, which described it as under development.

Last twelve months. The announcement of the law came on 9 December 2025, and the report that the Digital Code was under development followed on 16 March 2026.

Not held. Whether a body supervises data protection under a general law, whether any regulations exist and whether any decision has been made are not held. No dated event shows the Digital Code advancing or stalling.

TGO.short: Togo has a 2019 data protection law; its authority trained correspondents in 2026, but whether any sanction has been issued is not known.
TGO.summary:
Authority. Article 55 of the law creates a national authority, the Instance de protection des données à caractère personnel (IPDCP). The IPDCP officially launched its activities on 28 March 2025 in Lomé, and its head says it holds powers of control, injunction and sanction.

Standing. Loi n° 2019-014 of 29 October 2019 on the protection of personal data was adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated; article 95 gave State and public-service processing two years to comply and all other processing one year. On 15 September 2026 the IPDCP briefed ministry cabinet directors and secretaries-general on their obligations under it as data controllers.

Regulations. Article 58 of the law has the President of the Republic appoint the IPDCP's president by decree from its steering committee.

Application. The IPDCP gave attestations to 32 data protection correspondents on 24 June 2026 after three days of training in Adétikopé. On 15 September 2026 it convened public administrations in Lomé on prior formalities, declaration of existing processing and designation of correspondents.

Last twelve months. The IPDCP and the broadcast regulator HAAC signed a cooperation memorandum on 10 December 2025 that gives the IPDCP access to HAAC's monitoring room. The IPDCP opened its first evaluation and certification session for correspondents in Atakpamé on 30 September 2026, with 32 professionals.

Not held. No regulation made under the law is held. No named sanction or decision under it is held, and no published count of decisions.

TUN.short: A 2004 data protection law is in force and a replacement has been before parliament since 2025; whether the law is applied is not known.
TUN.summary:
Authority. The 2004 law names the Instance nationale de protection des données à caractère personnel and gives it the powers to receive declarations and to authorise processing and transfers. Government decree no. 2021-230 of 16 April 2021 appointed twelve members to it for three years: two members of parliament, two judges, ministry representatives, a human rights committee member and an ICT expert.

Standing. Organic law no. 2004-63 of 27 July 2004 on the protection of personal data sets the general regime for processing, consent and rights, and was the operative statute in September 2026. A draft organic law, no. 95/2025, was deposited before the Assembly of the Representatives of the People on 14 July 2025 and would repeal the 2004 law six months after publication.

Regulations. The law itself has the authority receive declarations and authorise processing and transfers.

Application. A representative of the authority was scheduled to be heard by the Assembly's Rights and Freedoms Committee on 25 February 2026, on the proposed new law.

Last twelve months. The Rights and Freedoms Committee scheduled a hearing of the sponsoring deputies on 17 February 2026 and began examining the articles of the bill's first title that month, a text that adds rules on artificial intelligence, surveillance cameras and health data. Tech Hive Advisory lists Tunisia among countries moving to amend an existing law in January and February 2026.

Not held. No regulation made under organic law no. 2004-63 is held, and no dated sanction, decision or count of decisions under it. The three-year term of the members appointed in 2021 has run out and no later appointment is held.

TZA.short: Tanzania's Personal Data Protection Act 2022, in force since 2023, was applied in a 2025 ruling; how many decisions have been made is not known.
TZA.summary:
Authority. The Act establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission as a body corporate, with a seven-member Board and a Director General. The Commission delivered a ruling on a complaint on 19 August 2025, and its Director General, Dr Emmanuel Mkilia, announced on-site inspections in Dodoma on 28 August 2026.

Standing. The Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 (Act No. 11 of 2022, Chapter 44) commenced on 1 May 2023 and applies to Mainland Tanzania and, for union matters, Zanzibar.

Regulations. The Personal Data Protection (Collection and Processing) Regulations, Government Notice No. 449C of 2023, apply alongside the Act. The Commission's ruling of 19 August 2025 applied regulation 17, on erasure, and regulation 18, on children's data in commercial advertisements.

Application. On 19 August 2025 the Commission ruled in Complaint No. PDPC/CMP/002/2025 against the operator of an Instagram business page, awarding the complainant TZS 20 million in damages, imposing a fine of TZS 5 million and ordering a newborn's photographs deleted within 14 days. Its preliminary assessments, reported on 28 August 2026, found inaccurate registration data and unlawful transfers of data abroad.

Last twelve months. On 8 January 2026 the Minister of Communication and Information Technology gave unregistered institutions a final three months to register and told the Commission to prepare nationwide compliance audits. On 11 February the Commission announced inspections from 9 April, on 12 June it gave institutions with incomplete registration seven days to finish, and on-site inspections began on 31 August.

Not held. No published count of the Commission's decisions for a stated year is held. The report of the August 2025 ruling does not name the respondent.

UGA.short: Uganda's Data Protection and Privacy Act is in force and was applied in decisions of 2025 and 2026; yearly decision counts are not known.
UGA.summary:
Authority. The Personal Data Protection Office is established under the Data Protection and Privacy Act and headed by a director, Baker Birikujja. It keeps a register of data collectors, controllers and processors.

Standing. The Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap 97, is in force. The office's director said in August 2026 that it requires data collectors and processors to register and makes failure to register a criminal offence. The office has held that the Act applies to foreign entities serving persons in Uganda.

Regulations. The office's decision of 20 February 2026 was made under the Data Protection and Privacy Regulations, 2021. Its decisions apply Regulation 15 on registration, Regulation 30 on cross-border transfers, Regulation 46 on appeal and Regulation 48 on offences.

Application. On 18 July 2025 the office found Google LLC in breach of the Act's registration and cross-border transfer duties and ordered it to register within 30 days. On 20 February 2026 it partly upheld a complaint and issued five corrective orders to WhatsApp LLC, with no fine.

Last twelve months. On 3 December 2025 a magistrate fined the finance manager of Vuka Africa Ltd sh100,000 for failing to register with the office. By letter of 17 July 2026 the office confirmed that WhatsApp LLC had implemented the corrective measures. In August 2026 its director said 14,697 of an estimated 50,000 entities required to register had done so.

Not held. No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled for a stated period. The year the Act was passed and the date it commenced are not given.

ZAF.short: South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act, 2013 has been in force since 2021 and is applied; the planned amendment's text is not known.
ZAF.summary:
Authority. The Information Regulator was established on 1 December 2016 to monitor and enforce the Act. Its annual report for the year to 31 March 2025 describes an independent body under section 39 of the Act.

Standing. The Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 was signed into law in 2013 and has been in force since 1 July 2021, after a year's grace period, with fines of up to R10 million.

Regulations. Regulations on the processing of health information, made under section 112(2)(c) of the Act, were published in Government Gazette 54268 on 6 March 2026 and commenced on publication. An enforcement notice of 21 February 2024 cites earlier regulations under section 112(2), which prescribe the form for direct-marketing consent.

Application. The Regulator reports that in 2024/25 it received 1,355 complaints under the Act and resolved 745 of them. Its first fine, in July 2023, was R5 million on the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development, and it issued an enforcement notice to WhatsApp LLC on 10 September 2024.

Last twelve months. On 20 May 2026 the Regulator published an enforcement notice against Central Johannesburg TVET College, and in August 2026 it issued one to the South African Bureau of Standards over a 2024 ransomware attack. A commissioner said on 18 August 2026 that work is under way with the justice department to amend the Act to cover artificial intelligence and privacy by design.

Not held. No bill or draft of the amendment to the Act. The dates of the fines on the Electoral Commission and Lancet Laboratories are not given.

ZMB.short: Zambia's Data Protection Act of 2021 is in force, applied so far through registration and training; whether any decision has been made is not known.
ZMB.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection Commissioner, Likando Luywa, spoke in June 2026 on oversight and the registration of data controllers and processors. A tender of 10 August 2026 seeks a firm to build a compliance management system for the Data Protection Commission of Zambia.

Standing. The law is the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021, which a tender of 10 August 2026 names as the Act being implemented. It was described in July 2026 as part of the legal framework businesses must comply with, and a World Bank appraisal document published on 5 September 2024 gives it as the standard for the Department of National Registration's personal-data procedures.

Regulations. A tender of 10 August 2026 seeks consultants to help the Commission develop regulatory instruments for implementing the Act.

Application. Data controllers and processors had until 30 April 2025 to register under the Act. UNDP, writing on 17 September 2024, listed training staff in more than 145 offices across 10 provinces on the Act as a requirement of the digital ID rollout. Lusaka Star reported on 7 June 2026 that enforcement and compliance remained a challenge.

Last twelve months. A World Bank-financed tender opened on 10 August 2026, with expressions of interest due on 21 August, for a three-month assignment to review and develop national data protection guidelines and compliance frameworks. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner joined Zambia's delegation to the ID4Africa conference in Abidjan, which ended on 15 May 2026.

Not held. No regulation made under the Act is on record, and the date the Act came into force is not stated. No decision, sanction or count of cases under the Act is on record; registration and training are the only application shown.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe has the Cyber and Data Protection Act of 2021, applied through licensing and notices; whether any controller has been sanctioned is not known.
ZWE.summary:
Authority. Section 5 of the Act designates the Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (POTRAZ) as the Data Protection Authority. Business Times reported in May 2026 that it has a Director for Data Protection and powers to audit, investigate, warn, direct and initiate prosecutions.

Standing. The Cyber and Data Protection Act, No. 5 of 2021, was gazetted on 11 March 2022. A June 2025 overview describes it as the main data protection law, applying to all public and private organisations, and in May 2026 it provided criminal sanctions for accountable officers, a fine or up to seven years in prison.

Regulations. The Minister of ICT made licensing regulations, Statutory Instrument 155 of 2024, under section 32 of the Act in September 2024. They require organisations processing the personal data of 50 or more people to hold a data controller licence, at US$50 to US$2,500 a year, with a first deadline of 12 March 2025.

Application. POTRAZ handed the first licences to 570 companies in June 2025, and the ICT minister said on 15 October 2025 that 721 controllers were licensed and 830 data protection officers trained. Its Director for Data Protection said in May 2026 that administrative sanctions were not yet in place.

Last twelve months. Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026, published in July 2026, announced mandatory compliance inspections of data controllers from 1 September 2026. In September 2026 POTRAZ consulted on guidelines under the Act and on amendments to the regulations covering administrative fines.

Not held. No named and dated sanction, order or decision on a controller, and no count of decisions for a stated period.

AGO.short: Law in force since 2011; the authority is appointed and working, and fined a hotel company in August 2026.
AGO.summary:
Law in force. Lei n.º 22/11 on personal data protection was published on 17 June 2011 and enters into force on the date of its publication. In June 2026 the Assembleia Nacional rejected a bill to amend it.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Angola ratified the Convention on 21 February 2020 and deposited its instrument on 11 May 2020.

Authority appointed. The Agência de Protecção de Dados was set up by Decreto Presidencial n.º 214/16 and Decreto Presidencial n.º 277/19 of 6 September 2019 appointed a president and two executive administrators to its board. In August 2026 its board took a sanction decision.

Implementing and acting. On 10 August 2026 the authority fined Lizária, Lda., owner of Hotel Diamante, the kwanza equivalent of USD 115,000 under Deliberação n.º 006/2026. Its register of fines lists 15 fines for 2022 to 2026, of US$75,000 to US$525,000 each.

Not held. No gap is recorded against the four questions.

BDI.short: A law was promulgated in March 2026; whether it is in force is not known, nor an appointed authority or any ruling.
BDI.summary:
Law in force. Burundi's National Assembly unanimously adopted a bill on personal data protection on 15 January 2026, covering the collection and processing of personal data across public and private sectors. It is structured in eight chapters, and the head of state promulgated the law on 10 March 2026, per Community Voice.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Burundi.

Authority appointed. The law establishes an independent administrative authority to oversee data protection, responsible for enforcement, and a dedicated body to implement and monitor data protection regimes.

Implementing and acting. DLA Piper's guide of 17 January 2024 described only sector confidentiality provisions in Burundi, before the 2026 law was adopted, and stated that no national data protection authority existed then.

Not held. Whether the law has entered into force, whether the authority has been constituted and whether it has ruled on any organisation are not established.

BEN.short: Law in force since 2018; the authority is appointed and working, and published figures for its decisions in 2025.
BEN.summary:
Law in force. Personal data protection in Benin sits in Book V of the Digital Code, law no. 2017-20 of 20 April 2018, which the APDP's 2015-2020 report gives as its legal framework. The code is amended by law no. 2020-35 of 6 January 2021, and La Nation of 5 September 2026 treats it as the current framework.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Benin ratified the Malabo Convention on 14 May 2024 and deposited its instrument on 12 November 2024.

Authority appointed. The Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles is established by Articles 462 to 473 of the Digital Code. Its president, Me Luciano Hounkponou, spoke at a forum in Johannesburg on 1 to 3 September 2026, and its 2026 budget programme is XOF 738,277,000.

Implementing and acting. The APDP's 2025 report gives 907 files examined, 64 inspection missions, 20 complaints treated and 75 compliance certificates issued. Its 2015-2020 report records 347 decisions rendered over 2016 to 2020, including the CNIL's refusal on 18 August 2016 of Spacetel Benin authorisation to collect biometric data.

Not held. No gap is recorded against the four questions.

BFA.short: Law in force since 2021; authority appointed and working; no ruling against an organisation is known.
BFA.summary:
Law in force. Law no. 001-2021/AN of 30 March 2021 abrogates law no. 010-2004/AN and gives one year from entry into force for all processing to comply. The CIL invoked it in a communiqué of 24 December 2024, and the CIL president recalled on 1 July 2025 that data protection is compulsory under it.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Burkina Faso.

Authority appointed. The Commission de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CIL) is led by its president, Dr Nassa, and was funded in 2024 under its own budget programme, XOF 857,062,000 appropriated and 93.3 percent executed. On 18 November 2025 its president signed the operational roadmap of the AES data protection authorities' coordination framework with Mali and Niger.

Implementing and acting. By communiqué of 24 December 2024 the CIL warned that repeated posting of people's images on social media without consent violates the law. On 1 July 2025 the Prime Minister launched CIL awareness sessions on personal data protection for ministries and public institutions, and on 26 June 2025 the CIL validated its public report for 2024.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

BWA.short: A data protection law has been in force since 2025, the commission is working, and it ruled against an organisation in 2026.
BWA.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024 came into operation on 14 January 2025. It applies to all organisations processing personal data, including public entities, Mmegi states.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Convention by Botswana.

Authority appointed. Mmegi reports Kepaletswe Somolekae as the newly appointed Information and Data Protection Commissioner on 11 February 2026. The Commission was established in 2022, and in July 2025 it had three contract officers, with the Deputy Commissioner and two director posts unfilled.

Implementing and acting. On 17 July 2026 the Commission issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice against DPSM, ordering the ePayslip portal suspended and a DPIA and revised privacy notice submitted within one month. Mmegi reports DPSM suspended the portal on 22 July 2026.

Not held. Nothing further on the four questions is held.

CAF.short: A data protection law is in force, but no authority is appointed, so none has ruled against an organisation, as of 2026.
CAF.summary:
Law in force. Data Protection Africa states in its factsheet of 28 January 2026 that the Central African Republic has a data protection law in place. The promulgated text of Loi n° 24.001, adopted in January 2024, gives no commencement date and no compliance period.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Convention by the Central African Republic.

Authority appointed. Data Protection Africa states the data protection authority had not yet been appointed as of 28 January 2026. Article 57 gives the ministry in charge of the digital economy twelve months from promulgation to set up the data protection agency, and names no composition, seat or financing for it.

Implementing and acting. The law's text vests the agency's missions in the ministry in charge of the digital economy until the agency is set up.

Not held. No source held says the Malabo Convention has been signed or ratified, or that an authority has been appointed. Nothing is held on how the law is applied or on any ruling.

CIV.short: A data protection law is in force and its authority is working, but no ruling against an organisation is known as of 2026.
CIV.summary:
Law in force. The law of 19 June 2013 on personal data protection is the framework under which a 2015 decree sets filing fees, prior authorisations and fines of up to FCFA 500 million on repeat breach. The digital minister cited the same law as the country's existing framework on 18 May 2026.

Malabo Convention. The African Union Commission's status list of 2 February 2026 records Côte d'Ivoire as having ratified or acceded to the Convention on 8 March 2023, with the instrument deposited on 3 April 2023.

Authority appointed. ARTCI, styling itself the Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles, issued a communique on 3 August 2026 inviting controllers to use CERTINUM. A fact sheet of 23 May 2022 says a data protection authority is appointed, with 7 members serving up to 6 years.

Implementing and acting. ARTCI launched Certinum on 2 July 2026, an online platform for compliance and processing-authorisation requests, replacing about 100 paper files handled each month. The minister listed compliance control operations carried out in 2022 and national awareness campaigns launched from 2015.

Not held. No ruling by the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

CMR.short: A data protection law came into force in 2026, but no authority is appointed, so no ruling against an organisation is known.
CMR.summary:
Law in force. The Direction Generale du Budget (Ministry of Finance) states that the deadline set for the entry into force of Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on personal data protection was reached on 23 June 2026, and that the law is now officially in force.

Malabo Convention. The African Union Commission's status list of 2 February 2026 records Cameroon as having signed the Convention on 12 August 2021, with no ratification or deposit date.

Authority appointed. The law defines the Autorité as an independent public body in charge of data protection and gives it supervision, notification and enforcement functions.

Implementing and acting. The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications told the National Assembly on 8 April 2025 that Cameroon had adopted the law of 23 December 2024, setting principles, controller obligations and data subject rights.

Not held. No ratification of the Malabo Convention is held, and no source held says an authority has been appointed. Nothing is held on how the law is applied or on any ruling.

COD.short: Since 2023 a data protection law is in force; no authority is appointed yet and no ruling against an organisation is known.
COD.summary:
Law in force. The Digital Code, Ordinance-Law No. 23/010 of 13 March 2023, entered into force in 2023 and provides for the Autorité de Protection des Données.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that the Democratic Republic of the Congo ratified the Malabo Convention on 6 March 2025 and deposited its instrument on 27 June 2025.

Authority appointed. Beto.cd reported on 13 September 2026 that the Autorité de protection des données is not installed. A ministerial order of 17 August 2024 provisionally gave its missions to ARPTIC pending its establishment. Its organisation and operation await a Prime Minister's decree.

Implementing and acting. On 12 March 2026 the Ministry of Digital Economy launched a national network of data protection officers in Kinshasa, backed by RUDI International and Droit-Numérique.cd, to standardise personal data practice and support compliance. No sanction or decision is reported.

Not held. No source dated in the last three years shows an appointed authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

COG.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority was appointed in 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
COG.summary:
Law in force. Law No. 29-2019 of 10 October 2019 on personal data protection is in force as of 22 January 2026, and Decree No. 2025-538 completes the institutional framework it established.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Congo ratified the Malabo Convention on 24 September 2020 and deposited its instrument on 23 October 2020.

Authority appointed. The National Personal Data Protection Commission was inaugurated in January 2026 after its members were appointed under Decree No. 2025-538 of 31 December 2025. Its President, Vice President and Rapporteur were elected at the inaugural meeting.

Implementing and acting. On 22 January 2026 ITWeb Africa reported that Congo-Brazzaville has established the Commission, whose members were installed by ICT minister Leon Juste Ibombo, who described it as an independent body able to advise, warn and sanction.

Not held. No source dated in the last three years shows an appointed authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

COM.short: A data protection law passed in 2021 is not known to be in force; no authority is appointed and no ruling is known.
COM.summary:
Law in force. TechHive Advisory states the Union of Comoros enacted its Protection of Personal Data Law on 29 June 2021 as a comprehensive framework. The Assembly adopted Loi n°14-029/AU on personal data protection, 68 articles, in plenary session on 26 June 2014.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Comoros signed the Malabo Convention on 29 January 2018 and had not ratified it.

Authority appointed. TechHive Advisory states the law establishes a National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data but that as of mid-2024 it had not been formally constituted or made operational. Article 19 of the 2014 law institutes a Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés whose nine members are named by decree under Article 24.

Implementing and acting. As of mid-2024, TechHive Advisory states the authority had not been formally constituted or made operational.

Not held. The evidence does not establish whether the law has commenced, whether the authority has been constituted since mid-2024, or any ruling against an organisation.

CPV.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority is working in 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
CPV.summary:
Law in force. The CNPD president says the base data protection law dates from 2001 and was amended in 2013 and in 2021, in an interview published 2 February 2025. The IBA chapter states Law 133/V/2001 is Cabo Verde's general data protection regime, applying within the country and to processing of data of people located in it.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Cape Verde ratified the Malabo Convention on 13 November 2020 and deposited its instrument on 5 February 2022.

Authority appointed. The CNPD, led by president Faustino Varela, started in 2015-2016 and completes a decade of existence in 2025. Resolução n.º 160/X/2024 appropriates CVE 36,313,115 for the CNPD in the Assembly's own budget for FY2025, up from CVE 35,255,451 in FY2024.

Implementing and acting. The CNPD president says cases have arrived involving AI and Big Data, including two generative-AI image manipulation cases, with cases that may be criminal sent to the Ministério Público; no decision or count is given. The CNPD's 2024 activity plan, dated 27 December 2023, covers planned inspections, guidance and international fora.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

DJI.short: A data protection law was passed in 2025 but is not in force; no authority is appointed or has ruled against an organisation.
DJI.summary:
Law in force. The National Assembly passed Djibouti's first Digital Code, with a data-protection regime embedded in it, on 30 June 2025. It was still to be promulgated by the President and published in the Journal Officiel. TechHive Advisory describes the regime as 156 articles in all, within the Code.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Djibouti signed the Convention on 12 May 2023 and had not ratified it.

Authority appointed. The Code creates the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data, independent with administrative and financial autonomy. Jones Day frames the competent authorities as still to be operationalised.

Implementing and acting. TechHive Advisory states that the regime was enacted in June 2025 as part of the Digital Code, and gives no promulgation or commencement date.

Not held. The date the Code was promulgated or took effect, whether the commission has been constituted, and any ruling by it.

DZA.short: The law is in force and the authority is working in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is reported.
DZA.summary:
Law in force. The US International Trade Administration states that Law No. 18-07, enacted on 10 June 2018, came into force on 10 August 2023. El Moudjahid reports that law 25-11, promulgated in July 2025, amends it with data protection delegate, processing register and operations log duties.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Convention by Algeria.

Authority appointed. The national authority, the ANPDP, adopted a deliberation on 15 July 2026 by a majority of its members, signed by its president, with twelve members named. El Moudjahid names Samir Bourehil as its president in July 2026.

Implementing and acting. The ANPDP's deliberation says it has put an online complaint service at the disposal of data subjects. Tech Hive Advisory reports a decision in early 2026 on employee drug test results, and a 2025 roundup reports a compliance package of guidelines and four templates.

Not held. Any ruling by the authority against a named organisation in the last three years.

EGY.short: The law is in force and an authority is appointed in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is reported.
EGY.summary:
Law in force. Baker McKenzie says Law No. 151 of 2020 is in a one-year compliance grace period that expires on 31 October 2026, by which date all data users must be in full compliance. Access Partnership says enforcement is expected from 1 November 2026.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Convention by Egypt.

Authority appointed. A 7 August 2026 report says the Personal Data Protection Centre, affiliated to the ICT ministry, is acting under Law 151 of 2020 with an acting chief executive. Baker McKenzie says it launched its electronic portal in early October 2026 for accreditation, licence and permit applications.

Implementing and acting. Tech Hive Advisory says the Centre published guidelines on consent, lawful bases, direct marketing and licences, and breach-notification templates, in January and February 2026.

Not held. Any ruling by the Centre against an organisation, and any inspection it has carried out.

ERI.short: No data protection law is in force and no authority is appointed in 2026, so none has ruled against an organisation.
ERI.summary:
Law in force. Law Lab Africa states that no comprehensive data protection law is in force in Eritrea, as of a verification pass on 1 August 2026. A June 2025 Horn of Africa Initiative update says Eritrea remains without data protection legislation.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Eritrea.

Authority appointed. Law Lab Africa states that no supervisory authority has been established in Eritrea, as of 1 August 2026. Levellers, reviewed on 8 June 2026, states that no data protection authority has been appointed.

Implementing and acting. Law Lab Africa states that no enforcement decisions could be found for Eritrea and none are published, as of the 1 August 2026 verification pass by that source.

Not held. Any draft data protection law, and any body with data protection duties.

ETH.short: Ethiopia published a data protection law in 2024 and its communications regulator oversees it; no ruling against an organisation is known.
ETH.summary:
Law in force. Ethiopia published its Personal Data Protection Proclamation in the Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024, and Shega reported in November 2025 that it took effect on publication.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Ethiopia.

Authority appointed. The Ethiopian Communications Authority is the regulator under Article 5 of the Proclamation, per the Tech Hive review; its Director General said in November 2025 that data processors and collectors now need the Authority's permission and that staffing and technical capacity are being expanded.

Implementing and acting. The Authority told Shega it had received about 10 requests to transfer data abroad and approved them as a temporary measure, and officials previewed a registration portal for data controllers and processors at a workshop co-hosted with Huawei.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

GAB.short: Gabon's data protection law was published in 2023, its authority is working, and it fined Citibank Gabon in 2024.
GAB.summary:
Law in force. Loi n°025/2023 of 12 July 2023 amended the 2011 data protection law with rights, controller duties, data protection officers, breach notification and sanctions, and was published in the Journal Officiel on 15 July 2023.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Gabon.

Authority appointed. The APDPVP sat in plenary on 25 April 2024 with a named president, vice-president and six other permanent commissioners, appointed by a Council of Ministers decision of 12 July 2023; its president, Joel Dominique Ledaga, spoke as its sitting head on 4 September 2026.

Implementing and acting. By deliberation n°073 of 25 April 2024, the APDPVP imposed a sanction of 90,000,000 FCFA on Citibank Gabon S.A. for diverting employee data from its declared purpose and processing ethnic-origin data. Its president said in September 2026 it had logged about 715 declarations of conformity and about 30 complaints from individuals.

Not held. Nothing is outstanding on the four questions.

GHA.short: Ghana's data protection law is in force and its commission is working in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
GHA.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) is the law the Data Protection Commission enforces, and a Circuit Court in Accra applied it in a judgment of 18 September 2024.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Ghana ratified the Malabo Convention on 13 May 2019 and deposited its instrument on 3 June 2019.

Authority appointed. The Data Protection Commission is led by Executive Director Dr Arnold Kavaarpuo, according to the Ghana News Agency in October 2026. A new Governing Board chaired by Teki Akuetteh was sworn in in August 2025, and the 2026 budget estimates appropriate GHS 9,720,400 to the Commission, which has 39 staff.

Implementing and acting. The Commission said in August 2026 that enforcement actions have begun and it had declared 2026 the "Year of Enforcement", and it said it would begin spot checks on registration and lawful processing from 5 October 2026. The Communications Minister reported a 98.4 per cent rise in newly registered data controllers in the first half of 2026.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

GIN.short: Guinea adopted a data protection law in 2016, but no authority is appointed and no ruling is known.
GIN.summary:
Law in force. At the closing of the Transform Africa Summit on 19 November 2025, Minister Rose Pola Pricemou said Guinea is strengthening its regulatory framework with a new data-protection law. The 2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law, Loi L/2016/037/AN, was adopted and promulgated by President Alpha Condé.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Guinea ratified the Malabo Convention on 31 July 2018 and deposited its instrument on 16 October 2018.

Authority appointed. The 2016 law defines an Autorité de Protection and sets its functions, including declarations, transfer approval and investigation. The CNT reported on 20 June 2024 that its commissions debated a bill to establish the authority, with the designation of members and their mandates still contested.

Implementing and acting. The bill to establish the authority was awaiting plenary adoption, the CNT reported on 20 June 2024.

Not held. No data protection law in force is held, and no authority constituted or appointed.

GMB.short: A law was enacted in 2025 but no start date is known; an authority is working; no ruling against an organisation is known.
GMB.summary:
Law in force. President Barrow assented the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025 on 7 November 2025, with no grace period before it becomes enforceable and no commencement date given.

Malabo Convention. The Gambia signed the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection on 2 December 2022 and the minister reiterated the government's commitment to ratify it; the African Union's list of 2 February 2026 records no ratification.

Authority appointed. The Information Commission of The Gambia is to develop a communication strategy raising awareness of the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025, per a notice published on 17 August 2026.

Implementing and acting. Paradigm Initiative says the Gambia enacted data protection legislation in September 2025 and calls for implementation and enforcement by the relevant authorities, in a press release dated 29 January 2026.

Not held. A commencement date for the Act, and any ruling against an organisation.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau has no data protection law in force in 2026 and no authority appointed; no ruling against an organisation is known.
GNB.summary:
Law in force. A professor at the Bissau Faculty of Law said on 22 September 2026 that Guinea-Bissau does not yet have specific data protection legislation, and a national report of 18 February 2025 lists a personal data protection bill awaiting discussion.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Guinea-Bissau signed the Malabo Convention on 31 January 2015 and had not ratified it.

Authority appointed. The professor said Guinea-Bissau has no dedicated national data protection authority, these matters being handled by several institutions sector by sector; a Data Protection Africa factsheet of 25 May 2022 gave the same finding.

Implementing and acting. The professor said a bill provides for creating a 'Data Protection Agency', with independence risks in its membership and in leaving its organisation to a decree.
