Not held. The stage of the bill, and any ruling against an organisation.

GNQ.short: A law has been in force since 2016, but its authority was not appointed as of 2022 and no ruling is known.
GNQ.summary:
Law in force. Ley Núm. 1/2016 of 22 July 2016 sets rules for personal data processing in the public and private sectors and enters into force twenty days after its publication in the Boletín Oficial del Estado.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's Infrastructure and Energy Department reports that Equatorial Guinea's foreign minister signed the Malabo Convention in Addis Ababa on 28 July 2026, as a step towards ratification.

Authority appointed. Articles 15 and 29 name the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body, to be created by a decree that will fix its structure.

Implementing and acting. Data Protection Africa (ALT Advisory) states that Law No. 1/2016 creates the Governing Body for the Protection of Personal Data as the data protection authority, but that it is not yet appointed or operational.

Not held. Ratification of the Malabo Convention is not held, nor is any appointment to the authority or any ruling against an organisation.

KEN.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is appointed and working; it has fined businesses since 2022.
KEN.summary:
Law in force. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner enforces the Data Protection Act and Regulations and has issued fines under it since 2022, and in a Senate statement on 13 May 2026 the ICT Cabinet Secretary said the Data Protection Act, 2019 is being enforced.

Malabo Convention. Citizen Digital reported on 8 September 2026 that Kenya had not yet formally joined the Malabo Convention: Cabinet approved it in 2025 and ratification awaits National Assembly approval.

Authority appointed. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was established under the Data Protection Act, 2019, with inaugural commissioner Immaculate Kassait in office since 2020; the ODPC bulletin of March 2025 shows the Office registering data handlers from offices in Nairobi, Kisumu, Mombasa, Eldoret, Machakos, Nyeri and Nakuru.

Implementing and acting. The ODPC bulletin states that as of March 2025 the Office had received 7,128 complaints, issued 215 determinations and imposed penalties on 10 entities, and Cadmus Cyber Solutions states the Office had fined at least nine businesses KES 26,275,000 in total by September 2024.

Not held. A completed ratification of the Malabo Convention.

LBR.short: A data protection law is in force from 2026; no authority is known to be working and no ruling against an organisation is known.
LBR.summary:
Law in force. Liberia's printed Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, approved on 9 March 2026 and printed on 23 March 2026, takes effect on publication into handbills (s.44), and existing businesses have one year from the effective date to comply (s.41).

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Liberia.

Authority appointed. Sections 8 and 10 of the Act give data protection functions to the Independent Information Commissioner, the oversight body created by the Freedom of Information Act of 2010; the Act does not state that the Commissioner has begun acting under it.

Implementing and acting. On 13 September 2026 the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection said that it is aware of its responsibilities under Liberia's Data Protection and Privacy Act, and that it took part in validating the legal framework.

Not held. The country has not ratified the Malabo Convention, and no source held says an authority has been appointed.

LBY.short: Whether a law is in force is not known as of 2026; no authority or ruling is known, so no stage is set.
LBY.summary: Not held. Nothing held says whether a data protection law is in force.

LSO.short: A data protection law is in force; the authority it creates has not been appointed, and no ruling against an organisation is known (2026).
LSO.summary:
Law in force. Cenfri says that Lesotho's Data Protection Act has been law for over a decade, in a document published on 23 March 2026.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Lesotho ratified or acceded to the Malabo Convention on 5 February 2025 and deposited its instrument on 16 February 2025.

Authority appointed. Cenfri says that the Data Protection Commission under Lesotho's Data Protection Act has remained unappointed, in its document published on 23 March 2026.

Implementing and acting. The law firm Z. Mayet and Associates states that the Act establishes a Data Protection Commission, but that the Commission and its Commissioner have not been appointed, in a document published on 31 October 2025.

Not held. No source dated in the last three years shows an appointed authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

MAR.short: Law 09-08 is in force and the CNDP authority is working, issuing guidance in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
MAR.summary:
Law in force. The president of the CNDP, interviewed on 4 August 2026, speaks of Law 09-08 as in force for more than fifteen years, with its paradigms still applicable.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Morocco.

Authority appointed. The CNDP, Morocco's national commission for the control of personal data protection, validated five new deliberations on 28 November 2025, acting as the supervisory body.

Implementing and acting. In a communiqué dated 28 August 2026, the CNDP gave guidance on Law 09-08 to political parties and voters for the 23 September 2026 elections, and opened a 3020 information line. It published a national register of notified processing operations in January 2023.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

MDG.short: A 2015 law is in force and its authority was sworn in during August 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
MDG.summary:
Law in force. Loi n° 2014-038 on the protection of personal data was promulgated on 9 January 2015, and the procedures manual of the data protection commission, dated December 2025, treats it as the operative legal basis for its work.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Madagascar ratified the Malabo Convention on 17 July 2025 and deposited its instrument on 15 September 2025.

Authority appointed. Seven members of the Commission Malagasy de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CMIL) were sworn in at the Cour suprême on 4 August 2025. Its bureau was elected on 14 August 2025, and in March 2026 the Unité de Gouvernance Digitale announced the CMIL is now effectively in place.

Implementing and acting. The CMIL's annual report of January 2026 says no processing declaration has been registered yet, that citizens' complaints went untreated for ten years, and that the commission has no premises or staff, with 104 posts targeted in the 2026 Finance Law.

Not held. No source dated in the last three years shows the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

MLI.short: Law 2013-015 is in force and its authority works; it fined a Bamako clinic and a company in 2025.
MLI.summary:
Law in force. Law no. 2013-015 of 21 May 2013, as amended, is the basis the authority's president cited for its sanctions when opening its session on 3 August 2026. A decree of 14 May 2024 is made under it.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Mali.

Authority appointed. The Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APDP) held its second ordinary session on 3 August 2026 under president Pr Mamoudou Samassekou with all commissioners present. It opened regional offices at Kayes, Sikasso, Segou and Mopti and a Ségou antenna on 4 December 2025.

Implementing and acting. In 2025 the APDP fined a Bamako clinic 5 million FCFA for obstructing a verification mission and fined Société Aminata Konaté SARL 5 million F CFA for refusing one. Sahel Tribune, summarising the 2025 annual report, reports fines totalling 22 million FCFA.

Not held. Nothing further on the four questions is held.

MOZ.short: No law is in force and no authority is appointed; a draft law is on parliament's October 2026 agenda. No ruling is known.
MOZ.summary:
Law in force. DLA Piper states, in a guide last modified on 17 February 2026, that Mozambique has no specific data protection legislation. The World Bank says the Data Protection Act had not been approved by Cabinet or submitted to Parliament as of October 2025, and on 1 October 2026 the Assembly's Standing Commission placed a draft law on the agenda of the session opening 28 October.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Mozambique ratified the Malabo Convention on 2 December 2019 and deposited its instrument on 21 January 2020.

Authority appointed. A June 2025 inception report states that Mozambique has no data regulatory authority. A review of the draft law says it designates the existing Regulatory Authority for ICT as the National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data.

Implementing and acting. The World Bank's October 2025 paper says the Data Protection Office is not yet established, which prevents its operationalisation, and that the project envelope for it was cut from US$18m to US$11m.

Not held. A law in force, an appointed authority and any ruling are not held.

MRT.short: A 2017 law is in force and its authority met monthly and took decisions in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
MRT.summary:
Law in force. Law 2017-020 of 22 July 2017 on personal data protection is applied in the authority's deliberation 002/2026 of 24 March 2026. Deliberation 005/2025 of 30 July 2025 is issued under it and requires controllers using foreign cloud services to seek authorisation.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Mauritania ratified the Malabo Convention on 19 April 2023 and deposited its instrument on 9 May 2023.

Authority appointed. The Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APD) held its ordinary monthly session on 30 June 2026 under its president, with its members and the Government Commissioner present. Its site lists monthly meetings of 25 March, 29 April and 6 May 2026, and its president was sworn in for a second term on 7 October 2026.

Implementing and acting. On 24 March 2026 the APD gave a favourable opinion, conditional on its remarks, on the joint decision authorising Maaden Mauritanie's Maadeni system. At its 29 April 2026 meeting it approved amendments to its transfer and cloud deliberations, and on 19 November 2025 it examined complaints 004-2025, 006-2025 and 007-2025.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

MUS.short: A law is in force and the authority is working; in 2024 it reported rejecting 12 cross-border transfers and closing 39 complaints.
MUS.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Office reports on its enforcement in 2024 of the Data Protection Act 2017, citing its sections on complaints, transfers, registration, certification and appeals. Commissioner Madhub describes the 2017 regime as the country's current law, after a first law in 2004 partly implemented in 2009. The office also submitted a draft Data Protection Bill to the ministry to amend the Act for European Commission adequacy.

Malabo Convention. Mauritius ratified the Malabo Convention on 6 March 2018 and deposited its instrument on 14 March 2018, according to the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. Drudeisha Madhub is named as Data Protection Commissioner, and the Data Protection Office has been operational since 16 February 2009. In January 2026 the Office co-led the launch of the National Data Strategy 2025-2029 with the ministry, and a June 2026 set of regulations give it roles in receiving data protection officer notifications within 14 days and certifying officers.

Implementing and acting. For January to December 2024 the Office reports 179 new complaints, 39 closed, 105 personal data breaches notified, 112 cross-border transfers authorised and 12 rejected, and four compliance inspections. It issued guidelines for the insurance sector and 3,076 registration certificates in 2024.

Not held. Nothing further on the four questions.

MWI.short: A law is in force and an authority is working; no ruling against an organisation is known as of 2026.
MWI.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 3 of 2024) was assented to on 31 January 2024 and published on 2 February 2024. The Authority's compliance guideline says it applies at once to non-Malawi controllers and to Malawi controllers of significant importance, and that other Malawi controllers and processors must comply from 3 June 2026.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Malawi.

Authority appointed. The guidelines state that the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority, MACRA, is the designated Data Protection Authority under the Act. Nyasa Times reports it convened a stakeholder consultation on draft regulations in Lilongwe in July 2026, with Daniel Chiwoni as Head of Data Protection. The World Bank said in November 2025 that MACRA had appointed an acting Data Protection Commissioner.

Implementing and acting. In October 2025 the Authority published guidelines on personal data breach notifications, with a 72-hour notice to the Authority and to data subjects, and a compliance guideline and checklist covering the Act's duties, data subject rights and cross-border transfers. GIZ ran a training-of-trainers programme with the Authority in September 2026.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

NAM.short: Namibia has no law in force and no authority appointed, so none has ruled against an organisation; a bill is being finalised in 2026.
NAM.summary:
Law in force. Minister Theofelus said in July 2026 that Namibia is finalising the Data Protection Bill. In January 2026 she said the bill had been through consultation and drafting and was ready for resubmission to the Cabinet Committee on Legislation for onward processing by Parliament. An opposition MP told the Windhoek Observer in August 2026 that Namibia has no data protection statute.

Malabo Convention. Namibia ratified the Malabo Convention on 25 January 2019 and deposited its instrument on 1 February 2019, according to the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. The ministry's revised draft Data Protection Bill of 2022 provides in its long title for establishing a Data Protection Supervisory Authority and its powers, duties and functions. Section 25 of the 2020 draft establishes the Data Protection Supervisory Authority of Namibia, with Part VII running to section 37.

Implementing and acting. Minister Theofelus said on 14 August 2025 that the ministry would table a Data Protection Bill in September 2025. In 2018 the Minister of ICT told Parliament that Namibia had embarked on developing Personal Data Protection and Cyber Security Bills.

Not held. No law in force, no appointed authority and no activity by one are held.

NER.short: A law is in force, but its authority was abolished by decree in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
NER.summary:
Law in force. The president of the High Authority for the Protection of Personal Data, HAPDP, said in an interview published on 28 July 2025 that law no. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 repealed and replaced the 2017 law as amended in 2019. The authority's consolidated text of April 2026 presents the law as the operative general law, amended by Law 2023-31 of 4 July 2023.

Malabo Convention. Niger ratified the Malabo Convention on 22 February 2022 and deposited its instrument on 16 March 2022, according to the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. Africa Data Protection reports that the government has by decree abolished the HAPDP and split its powers between the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior, in a report published on 13 June 2026. In July 2025 the HAPDP president said the authority had ten members and that its president took office on 18 September 2024.

Implementing and acting. The HAPDP president said in July 2025 that the authority processed 139 compliance files since September 2024, covering declarations, video-surveillance declarations, and processing and transfer authorisations, and ran four control missions in 2025 on mobile operators.

Not held. No authority appointed after the decree is held, and none registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

NGA.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working; it fined Multichoice Nigeria in 2025.
NGA.summary:
Law in force. The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 was signed by President Tinubu on 12 June 2023. In July 2026 the Federal High Court treated the Act as operative in a case against the Commission, and a federal circular dated 27 July 2026 directed all federal ministries, departments and agencies to comply with it.

Malabo Convention. Nigeria signed the Malabo Convention on 23 January 2024 and had not ratified it at the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. The Nigeria Data Protection Commission is a full data protection authority under the Act, according to its National Commissioner on 14 September 2026, when its new Abuja headquarters was commissioned. Voice of Nigeria names Vincent Olatunji as National Commissioner and CEO.

Implementing and acting. The Commission fined Multichoice Nigeria N766,242,500 in 2025 for violating the Act. Premium Times reports its Final Order against Meta imposed a $32.8 million fine, later set aside when the Federal High Court adopted a settlement. In August 2026 it opened an investigation into the University of Lagos, Lotus Bank and Hackerbella Ltd.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions is outstanding.

RWA.short: A data protection law has applied since 2023 and an authority registers controllers (2026); a ruling against an organisation is not known.
RWA.summary:
Law in force. Rwanda's Data Protection Act was introduced on 15 October 2021, and its two-year grace period ended on 15 October 2023, marking the transition to enforcement and accountability, according to a legal adviser writing in The New Times.

Malabo Convention. Rwanda ratified the Malabo Convention on 14 November 2019 and deposited its instrument on 21 November 2019, according to the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. The National Cyber Security Authority acts as the supervisory authority for personal data protection and privacy under the Data Protection Act, as Rwanda observed Data Privacy Week in January 2026. In July 2026 CIPESA stated that Rwanda's AI policy positions the Authority to oversee data protection compliance relevant to AI systems.

Implementing and acting. The New Times reported in January 2026 that over the last four years the Authority has registered data controllers and processors with registration certificates, trained over 100 public sector data protection officers, and run sector workshops for pharmacists and local government entities.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

SDN.short: Sudan has no data protection law in force in 2026; two authorities set up by decree in 2025 have issued no binding rules.
SDN.summary:
Law in force. On 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers discussed a draft data and artificial intelligence bill and directed further study before approval by the interim parliament. On 11 August 2026 the Justice Ministry's under-secretary said the ministry is preparing a 2026 Law on Regulating Data and Artificial Intelligence with the digital transformation ministry. The Sudanese Center for Policy Studies says Sudan has no privacy law governing personal data and that a 2018 draft bill was never enacted.

Malabo Convention. Sudan signed the Malabo Convention on 15 March 2023 and had not ratified it at the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. The Sudanese Center for Policy Studies says the Sudanese Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority and the Sudanese Cybersecurity Authority were both established by a November 2025 decree.

Implementing and acting. According to the same Center, citing the AI Regulation Tracker, neither of those two authorities had issued binding rules as of mid-2026.

Not held. Any ruling by an authority against an organisation, and the content of the draft bill.

SEN.short: A 2008 data protection law is in force and the authority is working; it ordered a company to remove a camera in March 2026.
SEN.summary:
Law in force. A reference summary states that Law No. 2008-12 on the protection of personal data was enacted on 25 January 2008 and has been in force since 2014. In April to June 2026 the Commission issued receipts, authorisations and a rejection under that law. An expert told APS in March 2026 that a bill to replace it is reportedly in the circuit.

Malabo Convention. Senegal ratified the Malabo Convention on 3 August 2016 and deposited its instrument on 16 August 2016, according to the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. The Commission de protection des données personnelles (CDP) is an independent administrative authority set up by Law No. 2008-12. It held two plenary sessions in April to June 2026, and its president signed a partnership convention with Benin's authority in April 2026.

Implementing and acting. On 12 March 2026 the CDP, after a complaint, inspected Digicommunication International unannounced and ordered the meeting-room camera uninstalled. For April to June 2026 it reported 195 files handled, 39 authorisations issued and one processing rejected. In 2024 it served a formal notice on SOLID SA, operator of the Kay Voter platform.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions is outstanding.

SLE.short: In 2026 the data protection law is still a draft bill and no authority is appointed; no ruling against an organisation is known.
SLE.summary:
Law in force. Sierra Leone has a Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill, which the Information Minister said in November 2025 had finished its final national validation, with Cabinet and Parliament still to come. In April 2026 Cabinet approved a National Data Protection Policy and authorised a new Data Protection and Right to Access Information Act.

Malabo Convention. Sierra Leone signed the Malabo Convention on 29 January 2016, and the African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that it had not ratified it.

Authority appointed. The 2025 Bill would establish for the first time a single independent authority for both data protection and access to information, and that authority is not yet constituted because the Bill is unenacted.

Implementing and acting. Cabinet's April 2026 decision left the Ministry of Information and Civic Education and the Attorney-General's office to finalise the Bill and table it in Parliament.

Not held. Whether any authority is constituted or acting is not held, and neither is any ruling against an organisation.

SOM.short: Somalia's data protection law is in force and an authority is appointed and taking registrations since 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
SOM.summary:
Law in force. Somalia's Data Protection Act, Law No. 005 of 2023, was enacted on 23 March 2023 and became effective immediately, according to TechHive Advisory. In June 2026 the Authority's notice required registration under Article 32 of the Act from all entities that collect, store, process or share personal data in Somalia.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Somalia.

Authority appointed. Somalia inaugurated its Data Protection Authority on 24 February 2024. Its own service page of 2 June 2026 lists the registration forms it issues, and its January 2026 Registration Guidelines set fees and a 30-day approval timeline.

Implementing and acting. On 2 June 2026 the Authority began accepting registration applications from controllers and processors and said it will issue certificates only to those meeting the conditions. In February 2024 it published guidelines for implementing the law.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

SSD.short: In 2026 South Sudan's data protection law is still a draft bill; no authority is appointed and no ruling against an organisation is known.
SSD.summary:
Law in force. A two-day workshop of over 30 stakeholders, convened by Digital Rights Frontlines with the NCA, reviewed the Data Protection Bill, 2025 in a post dated 5 May 2026. The ICT Minister said in December 2025 the government will introduce its first Data Protection Bill in 2026. The World Bank's 2026 diagnostic states there is no national data protection or privacy law.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by South Sudan.

Authority appointed. Digital Rights Frontlines states in February 2026 that the country lacks a fully operational, independent Data Protection Authority. Radio Tamazuj reports the draft bill, once passed, will establish a Data Protection Commission.

Implementing and acting. In October 2025 Paradigm Initiative and Koneta Hub held a two-day Juba convening of lawmakers, civil society and officials to seek parliamentary commitment to table the draft Bill.

Not held. No enacted data protection law, no operating authority and no ruling against an organisation is held.

STP.short: The 2016 data protection law is in force; the authority, appointed, signed a cooperation agreement in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
STP.summary:
Law in force. The IBA chapter of 2024 names the Personal Data Guarantee and Protection Law, Law 03/2016, as the primary instrument, covering processing by controllers headquartered or established in the country. Lei n.º 03/2016 was published in the Diário da República of 10 May 2016.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that São Tomé and Príncipe ratified or acceded on 25 September 2023 and deposited its instrument on 15 February 2024.

Authority appointed. The Agência Nacional de Protecção de Dados Pessoais has a president, José Manuel Costa Alegre. In April 2026 he met the National Assembly president to plan oversight of personal data in the electoral roll, and on 1 June 2026 the agency signed a cooperation memorandum with Macau.

Implementing and acting. The IBA chapter describes the fines and criminal sanctions the law provides and says the agency imposes fines and ancillary measures. In January 2025 its president described working with Facebook on fake profiles.

Not held. No source dated in the last three years shows the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. No ruling against an organisation is held.

SWZ.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working; it has ruled against named organisations, most recently in 2025.
SWZ.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act, 2022 was gazetted on 4 March 2022. The Ministry of ICT referred to its implementation and enforcement as current in August 2026, and enforcement notices under section 41 of the Act run to March 2025.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Eswatini. In July 2026 the Minister of ICT presented to a Senators' workshop on the importance of ratifying it.

Authority appointed. The notice of 2024 states the Act designates the Eswatini Communications Commission as the Eswatini Data Protection Authority. The Ministry of ICT vests oversight of compliance in it, and it has powers to investigate breaches, resolve complaints and impose sanctions. In September 2026 it was led by an acting chief executive.

Implementing and acting. The Authority issued enforcement notices under section 41 in June 2024 to MTN Eswatini and Liberty Life Swaziland Limited and in March 2025 to the Royal Science Technology Park. Registration of controllers and processors became mandatory on 1 March 2024. In June 2026 it opened a formal investigation into the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Not held. Nothing further is held on the four questions.

SYC.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working, handling 14 cases in 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
SYC.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act, 2023 was assented to on 19 December 2023 and bears the operative date 22 December 2023. The Commission's page states the Act came into effect, and Appleby reports an 18-month transition for controllers and processors from that date.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Seychelles.

Authority appointed. The Information Commission is named in section 5 as the competent authority, with powers to investigate, audit, issue enforcement notices and impose administrative fines up to SCR200,000. In 2025 it had a Chief Information Commissioner, two Information Commissioners and a CEO in post, and it took on the mandate at the end of December 2023.

Implementing and acting. The Commission handled 14 cases under the Act in 2025: 6 on data transfers, 5 breaches, 2 refused deletion requests and 1 consultation. In 2024 it received four data protection cases, mostly from the non-banking financial sector. In 2026 it marked Data Protection Day with guidance to organisations and the public.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

TCD.short: A digital law covering data protection was still being finalised in March 2026; no authority or ruling is known.
TCD.summary:
Law in force. A digital law covering data protection is still being finalised. Minister Boukar Michel announced on 9 December 2025 that authorities are finalizing a digital law incorporating international standards on cybersecurity, data protection and internet governance. Ecofin reports the Digital Code has been under development since December 2025 and incorporates international standards on cybersecurity and data protection.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Chad signed the Malabo Convention on 14 June 2015 and had not ratified it.

Authority appointed. Ecofin reports that Chad's Digital Code, under development since December 2025, incorporates international standards on cybersecurity and data protection.

Implementing and acting. The Minister's announcement of 9 December 2025 concerned a digital law still being finalised, with data protection among the standards it incorporates. Ecofin's report of 16 March 2026 still describes the Code as under development.

Not held. The evidence does not show a data protection law in force, an authority appointed or any ruling.

TGO.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
TGO.summary:
Law in force. Loi n° 2019-014 of 29 October 2019 on personal data protection was adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated. In September 2026 the IPDCP briefed ministry cabinet directors and secretaries-general on their obligations as data controllers under it, and in June 2026 it said 35 data protection correspondents had been designated under the law.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Togo ratified or acceded to the Malabo Convention on 30 September 2021 and deposited its instrument on 19 October 2021.

Authority appointed. The IPDCP became operational in 2024 and, per its head, holds powers of control, injunction and sanction. It officially launched its activities in Lomé on 28 March 2025, and in 2026 it ran the June correspondent training and signed a cooperation agreement with Mali's APDP on 23 September.

Implementing and acting. The IPDCP ran a three-day training for 35 data protection correspondents from 22 to 24 June 2026 and opened its first evaluation and certification session for correspondents in Atakpamé on 30 September 2026, with 32 professionals. On 15 September 2026 it convened a compliance meeting for public administrations. It launched a public-awareness campaign in March 2025.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

TUN.short: A 2004 law is in force; an authority appointed in 2021 is reported at a standstill in 2026, with no ruling against an organisation known.
TUN.summary:
Law in force. Organic law no. 2004-63 of 27 July 2004 sets the general processing, consent and rights regime, and a Forum Chawki Gaddes statement of 3 October 2026 cites it as the law guaranteeing personal data protection. A replacement bill, no. 095/2025, was deposited before the Assembly on 14 July 2025. It would repeal the 2004 law six months after publication.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Tunisia signed on 23 April 2019 and had not ratified.

Authority appointed. Government decree no. 2021-230 of 16 April 2021 appointed twelve named members to the national personal data protection authority for three years. Decree no. 2020-312 of 15 May 2020 puts the citizen-ID register under its control.

Implementing and acting. The Forum Chawki Gaddes says in a statement of 3 October 2026 that the activities of the authority, INPDP, are at a standstill and calls for its reactivation.

Not held. No source dated in the last three years shows the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. No ruling against an organisation is held.

TZA.short: A data protection law has been in force since 2023, the Commission is working, and it ruled against a company in 2025.
TZA.summary:
Law in force. The Personal Data Protection Act, Chapter 44, commenced on 1 May 2023 and applies to Mainland Tanzania and, for union matters, Zanzibar. The Citizen reported on 28 August 2026 that the Commission will inspect compliance with the Act from 31 August 2026.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Tanzania.

Authority appointed. Section 6 of the Act establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission as a body corporate. Director General Dr Emmanuel Mkilia announced on-site inspections in Dodoma on 28 August 2026. The Commission ran the eighth phase of its DPO training in Morogoro on 7-8 October 2026.

Implementing and acting. PDPC figures cited in October 2026 show 15,146 institutions registered and 445 complaints received by August 2026. A ruling reported in August 2025 awarded TZS 20,000,000 against Mi Casa Company Limited and ordered deletion of personal data. FB Attorneys reports a ruling of 19 August 2025 with TZS 20 million damages, a TZS 5 million fine and deletion of a newborn's photos within 14 days.

Not held. No sanction is named in the 2026 registration and inspection reports.

UGA.short: A data protection law is in force, the Personal Data Protection Office is working, and it ruled against Google in 2025.
UGA.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap 97, was applied by the Personal Data Protection Office in its decision of 18 July 2025 as law in operation, including its reach over foreign entities handling Ugandans' personal data. The PDPO director says the Act requires registration of data collectors and processors and makes failure to register a criminal offence.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Uganda. Police forensic-services director Andrew Mubiru said on 12 August 2026 that Uganda has not ratified it and needs to domesticate it.

Authority appointed. The Personal Data Protection Office is headed by director Baker Birikujja, who addressed an ISACA Kampala breakfast on 18 August 2026. It briefed government IT officers on data protection on 13 August 2026.

Implementing and acting. The PDPO's decision of 20 February 2026 partly upheld a complaint against WhatsApp LLC and Meta Platforms and issued corrective orders; on 17 July 2026 it confirmed WhatsApp had implemented them. On 18 July 2025 it found Google in breach and ordered it to register within 30 days.

Not held. The director names no case taken to court.

ZAF.short: A data protection law has been in force since 2021; the Information Regulator is working and issued an enforcement notice to a college in 2026.
ZAF.summary:
Law in force. ITWeb reports that the Protection of Personal Information Act came into force on 1 July 2021 after a year-long grace period, with fines up to R10 million and up to 10 years' imprisonment.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records South Africa as having signed on 16 February 2023, with no ratification or accession date.

Authority appointed. The Information Regulator was established on 1 December 2016 and its chairperson Pansy Tlakula spoke for it in September 2026. Parliament's Justice Committee published candidate names for vacant positions on 11 September 2026. National Treasury appropriated R135.7m for 2025/26 to the Regulator.

Implementing and acting. The Regulator received over 8,000 security-compromise reports to date, 1,220 of them since April 2026. It issued the South African Bureau of Standards an enforcement notice in August 2026 giving it 90 days to revise policies and implement security measures. Its first fine, R5 million, was imposed on the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development in July 2023.

Not held. The Regulator's work with the justice department to amend POPIA for artificial intelligence has no bill or draft described.

ZMB.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority is appointed and working; no ruling against an organisation is known in 2026.
ZMB.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 is the law a World Bank tender notice of 10 August 2026 treats as being implemented. A July 2026 report describes it as part of the operating legal framework beside the Cyber Security Act and Cyber Crimes Act.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records Zambia as having ratified the Malabo Convention on 15 December 2020 and deposited its instrument on 24 March 2021.

Authority appointed. The first Data Protection Commissioner was appointed in June 2023. In September 2025 the Commissioner and a Deputy Commissioner took part in a review of a draft health data statutory instrument.

Implementing and acting. The Commissioner's office opened online registration for controllers and processors, with a 30 April 2025 deadline. UNDP lists training staff in over 145 offices across 10 provinces on the Act as a requirement of the digital ID rollout.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

ZWE.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority is appointed and working; no ruling against an organisation is known in 2026.
ZWE.summary:
Law in force. The Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] is applied through SI 155 of 2024, which took effect in September 2024 and made a Data Controller Licence mandatory. Business Times states the Act provides criminal sanctions for accountable officers.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Zimbabwe.

Authority appointed. POTRAZ states it is the designated Data Protection Authority under section 5 of the Act and is acting as such. Section 6(2) says it is not subject to the direction or control of any person in exercising its functions.

Implementing and acting. POTRAZ handed over the first Data Controller Licences to 570 companies in June 2025. In December 2025 it reported 831 organisations recognised as compliant. Its Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026 announces mandatory compliance inspections from 1 September 2026.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

AGO.short: No national digital strategy is on record for Angola, only a public administration digitalisation agenda and a World Bank programme, so no stage is set.
AGO.summary: Not held. No national digital strategy is held for Angola. The public administration agenda, the World Bank programme and the draft law on artificial intelligence are other kinds of instrument.

BDI.short: The World Bank stated in 2020 that Burundi has no national digital strategy, and whether one is now in preparation is not known.
BDI.summary:
Governance and finance. The World Bank's 2020 assessment recommends that the government adopt a national digital strategy as a pillar of its development plan, stating that the country lacks an overarching and cohesive one.

Standing. The World Bank's Burundi Digital Economy Assessment, published in 2020, states that Burundi lacks an overarching and cohesive digital strategy.

Text. The same 2020 assessment states there is no overarching digital economy strategy beyond the ICT policy PNDTIC 2010-2025.

Period. The nearest instrument is the ICT policy PNDTIC, which runs from 2010 to 2025.

Delivery plan. The 2020 assessment states that PNDTIC 2010-2025 lacks an actionable operational plan.

Reporting. The 2020 assessment names PNDTIC 2010-2025 as the only overarching instrument it finds.

Last twelve months. The latest statement held is the World Bank's 2020 assessment, which recommends adopting a new overarching strategic vision.

Not held. Both statements date from 2020 and nothing newer repeats them. No national digital strategy is on record as adopted, launched or in preparation.

BEN.short: Benin has a digital strategy to 2031 in preparation since February 2026, but whether it will be adopted or published is not known.
BEN.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Digital and Digitalisation ran the 5-6 February 2026 seminar that drafted the vision for the Stratégie numérique du Bénin 2031, with Deloitte.

Standing. The strategy is in preparation: on 24 March 2026 ASIN's director general said the agency was supporting the digital ministry in drawing it up, after consultations began at a Cotonou workshop on 5-6 February 2026. It follows a 2021-2026 digital strategy, described by a GSMA study published in January 2025.

Text. The February 2026 seminar was to end in a strategic reference document.

Period. The strategy runs to 2031, drawn up under the Ministries of Economy and Finance and Digital Affairs, where its predecessor covers 2021-2026.

Delivery plan. The seminar was to set the vision and priority initiatives for the next five years, with Deloitte giving technical support.

Reporting. The consultations launched in February 2026 cover internet coverage, e-services, artificial intelligence, digital skills and financing.

Last twelve months. The 5-6 February 2026 seminar brought public sector, private operators and technical partners together to define the vision and priority initiatives.

Not held. No adopting act, public text, period, plan or reporting is held for the 2031 strategy. The 2021-2026 strategy is only announced, with no adopting act or public text.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso adopted a digital economy strategy in 2018, running to 2027, but whether its text is published is not known.
BFA.summary:
Governance and finance. The health ministry's plan lists SN@DEN 2018-2027 with objectives covering its governance, digital trust and broadband.

Standing. The ministry's diagnostic report lists SN@DEN 2018-2027 as adopted on 6 June 2018, and the government presented a twelve-project roadmap to 2030 on 25 August 2025.

Text. The health ministry's plan lists SN@DEN among national strategies, with objectives for public administration, economic sectors and human capital.

Period. SN@DEN is listed with a period of 2018-2027, and a long-term digital strategy toward 2030 was described as current in March 2026.

Delivery plan. A Schéma directeur d'aménagement numérique was produced within the 2017-2020 action plan of SN@DEN, according to an article of 17 September 2021.

Reporting. The same 2021 article is the nearest held row, naming the Schéma directeur as the product of the 2017-2020 action plan.

Last twelve months. The health ministry's plan, dated January 2025, still lists SN@DEN with a period of 2018-2027.

Not held. No published text of SN@DEN is held. The 2030 roadmap is described only as announced or presented, with no adopting act, and no public text of it is held.

BWA.short: Botswana's cabinet adopted its digital transformation strategy in February 2020, running to 2026, but whether its text is published is not known.
BWA.summary:
Governance and finance. The ITU repository names the Ministry of Communications as lead of the SmartBots Digital Transformation Strategy, and the first phase of one of its projects cost government P234 million in 2023.

Standing. The government online coordinator said the strategy was adopted by cabinet in February 2020, and in September 2026 the President said it would be formally launched in November 2026.

Text. A January 2026 data-centre briefing says the strategy was established to enhance connectivity, build a knowledge workforce and digitalise services.

Period. The ITU repository gives the strategy's time frame as 2021-2026.

Delivery plan. The President said in September 2026 that the strategy and action plan would be formally launched in November 2026.

Reporting. A EUR 4.85 million project running August 2024 to August 2027 supports a monitoring and evaluation framework and a progress dashboard for the strategy.

Last twelve months. On 23 September 2026 the President told the UN Economic Commission for Africa that the strategy and action plan would be formally launched in November 2026.

Not held. No published text of the strategy is held, and no delivery plan or progress report is held. The 2021-2026 period comes from a third-party repository.

CAF.short: The Central African Republic had a national digital plan in drafting in 2021, for 2020 to 2025, and whether it was adopted is not known.
CAF.summary:
Governance and finance. The World Bank assessment says technical assistance for the Digital CAR strategy is financed under the Central African Backbone project, co-funded by the European Union and the African Development Bank.

Standing. A workshop on 10-11 November 2021, opened by the chief of staff of the Ministry of Digital Economy, Posts and Telecommunications, presented the studies for the Plan National Stratégique Centrafrique Digitale 2025.

Text. The November 2021 workshop presented the studies for the plan, which is the nearest held row to a text.

Period. The workshop document gives the plan's period as 2020-2025.

Delivery plan. The World Bank assessment of 2020 lists the strategy as in preparation, with technical assistance commissioned by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications.

Reporting. The 2020 assessment says a feasibility study on the digital strategy was launched in 2020 under the Central African Backbone project.

Last twelve months. The latest held row is the November 2021 workshop presenting the plan's studies.

Not held. Nothing after November 2021 is held on the plan, and no adoption or public text is held. Its stated period, 2020-2025, has ended.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire has a published digital strategy for 2021-2025, now past its period, and a 2025 successor whose adoption is not known.
CIV.summary:
Governance and finance. The published text has the Commission Nationale de Développement de la Société de l'Information steer the Stratégie nationale de développement du numérique 2021-2025, with a monitoring committee led by the digital ministry. Paradigm Initiative ties national allocations of about USD 91 million for 2024 and USD 101 million for 2025 to its cycle.

Standing. Fraternité Matin reports it adopted in January 2022. Its successor, the Stratégie nationale de transformation numérique 2025-2035, was validated at a workshop on 19-22 August 2025.

Text. The ministry published the strategy's own text, version 1.4 of 26 January 2022, on its site.

Period. The strategy covers 2021-2025, with 2025 targets for its 36 strategic indicators. The successor is named for 2025-2035.

Delivery plan. The action plan for seven pillars lists projects with start date, priority and budget in million FCFA, such as 95,000 million FCFA to connect public administrations to the national broadband network.

Reporting. We Are Tech Africa credited the strategy on 15 July 2025 with over 5,207 km of fibre, several online service portals and an operational National Cybersecurity Agency.

Last twelve months. A workshop on 3 September 2026 opened work toward 700 digital public services and a paper-free state by 2030.

Not held. No adopting act is on record for the strategy or for its successor. Whether the successor's text is public is not known.

CMR.short: Cameroon has a published digital plan adopted in 2016 whose period has ended, and an update in preparation, so progress is not known.
CMR.summary:
Governance and finance. The Plan stratégique Cameroun numérique 2020 assigns delivery to the postal and telecommunications ministry with the other ministries, ANTIC, ART and CAMTEL. Its financing column draws on the public investment budget, the telecommunications special fund and the State budget, alongside external financing.

Standing. The plan, dated May 2016, calls itself the adopted strategic plan and names no adopting act. A workshop on 3 July 2025 discussed the diagnostic for updating it, with the next step to follow government approval.

Text. The plan's full text, 72 pages, is published on the ministry's site.

Period. The plan began in 2016 and, on both its own text and the ITU repository, ended by 2025.

Delivery plan. The priority action plan lists projects per axis with indicators, 2020 targets and an amount in FCFA each, such as 125,000,000,000 for a broadband backbone extension.

Reporting. The plan assigns monitoring and evaluation to the PPBS committees of each administration and their monitoring-evaluation cells.

Last twelve months. The ITU repository lists Digital Cameroon 2020 as the country's strategy in its 2025 edition.

Not held. The update of the plan has no text or period yet. No report against the plan is held.

COD.short: DR Congo validated a national digital plan in 2019, now past its period, and a 2026 successor whose adoption is not known.
COD.summary:
Governance and finance. Paradigm Initiative lists the Presidency, the posts and telecommunications ministry and the regulator ARPTC as lead institutions of the Plan National du Numérique Horizon 2025, and reports public digital budget allocations of USD 103.7 million in 2025. The plan leaves its own budget to the Government and the ADN.

Standing. The national validation workshop of 3-5 September 2019 validated the plan, and no cabinet act is named. Its successor, the Politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique 2026-2030, was validated on 4 August 2026 and is due before the Council of Ministers.

Text. The full text, dated September 2019, is on the Presidency's site.

Period. The plan carries the strategy to the horizon 2025, with target years from 2020 to 2025.

Delivery plan. Its timetable gives 68 priority projects with indicators, baselines and targets dated 2020 to 2025.

Reporting. Agence Ecofin reported on 11 October 2025 that the ministry estimates the plan is about 60% complete.

Last twelve months. The Government's action programme for 2024-2028 sets putting the plan's remaining projects into action, and the successor was technically validated on 21-22 July 2026.

Not held. No adopting act is on record for the plan or for its successor. The successor has no action plan, steering body or monitoring yet, and the plan's progress is a ministry estimate.

COG.short: Congo adopted Vision Congo Digital 2025 by decree in 2019; its successor is awaiting approval, and its action plan and monitoring are not known.
COG.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy is mandated to implement Vision Congo Digital 2025, coordinated by an inter-ministerial committee, according to the World Bank appraisal of 11 May 2022.

Standing. Décret n° 2019-150 of 17 June 2019 approves the strategy. A successor, Stratégie numérique 2030, was reported complete on 13 October 2025 and awaits review and final approval by decree.

Text. The decree was published in the Journal officiel of 4 July 2019.

Period. The ITU repository gives the time frame as 2021 to 2025, while the successor is named Vision Congo digital 2030.

Delivery plan. A December 2020 World Bank diagnostic says the action plan was still being drawn up with consultants.

Reporting. The May 2022 appraisal lists monitoring and evaluation mechanisms among the requirements for implementing the strategy.

Last twelve months. A digital identity workshop in July 2025 was described as a milestone in implementing Congo Digital 2025.

Not held. No public text of Vision Congo Digital 2025, no monitoring and no domestic budget line for it are shown. Its successor is validated at ministry level but not adopted by decree, with World Bank finance only.

COM.short: Comoros adopted a public, costed digital strategy to 2028 in 2018; results against its targets are not known.
COM.summary:
Governance and finance. ANADEN, the national digital development agency created in 2019, has the implementation of Comores Numérique 2028 as its first mission, and the strategy itself designs a national digital council and an observatory.

Standing. The digital health strategy says the Government drew up Comores Numérique 2028 and adopted it in 2018.

Text. The text is public on ANADEN's site.

Period. Its roadmap runs from 2018 to 2028.

Delivery plan. The strategy costs its six axes at 52,995,160,485 KMF, planned costings of 2018, and a 2025 report gives a target of 5% of GDP for the digital sector by 2028.

Reporting. The strategy designs a national digital observatory to measure sector performance.

Last twelve months. On 25 August 2026 the minister said ANADEN is to contribute to implementing the strategy across the economy.

Not held. No published report on results against the strategy's targets, no domestic budget line for it and no adopting act are shown.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde approved a digital economy strategy to 2030 in 2024; its public text, plan and reporting are not known.
CPV.summary:
Governance and finance. On 25 November 2025 the Estratégia para a Economia Digital de Cabo Verde was presented to the Conselho Consultivo da Economia Digital, chaired by the Vice-Prime Minister.

Standing. Resolução 72/2026 lists it as approved in September 2024. The Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035 is in preparation, as that resolution only establishes its bases.

Text. The same resolution lists the strategy with a focus on competitiveness, innovation and the digital economy.

Period. It covers 2025 to 2030.

Delivery plan. NOSi's March 2020 action plan names three hubs for the strategy: connectivity, capacity-building and service provision.

Reporting. The same NOSi plan says implementation is under way with African Development Bank and World Bank support.

Last twelve months. The strategy was presented to the digital economy council on 25 November 2025, and the 2035 agenda's consultation followed on 6 August 2026.

Not held. No public text of the strategy and no plan, reporting, body or finance for it are shown. The Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035 is in preparation and not adopted, and the 2019 to 2021 Agenda has ended.

DJI.short: A national digital strategy was still to be written in October 2025, but later mentions leave its status not known, so no stage is set.
DJI.summary: Not held. The Council of Ministers of 7 October 2025 listed a national digital strategy as still to be drawn up, while later mentions of a Smart Nation strategy and a decision to update it give no status or date. Whether any national digital strategy has been adopted, or is in preparation, is not known.

DZA.short: Algeria adopted its national digital transformation strategy for 2025 to 2030 in May 2025, but costs and results against its targets are not known.
DZA.summary:
Governance and finance. The High Commission for Digitalisation, created by presidential decree 23-314 of 6 September 2023, designs the strategy and follows its implementation, and on 4 May 2026 it signed a project with UNDP, supported by the Government of Japan to support its implementation.

Standing. El Chaab says the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 was adopted, approved and published in May 2025, and on 12 May 2025 the High Commissioner called it the approved strategy.

Text. The text is published on the High Commission's site, in an August 2024 version with twenty-five strategic objectives.

Period. The ITU repository gives its time frame as 2025 to 2030.

Delivery plan. The minister said on 4 May 2026 that the implementation plan for 2025-2026 is under way, with an executive plan for 2027-2030 in preparation.

Reporting. The High Commission published a review of April 2024 to September 2026 listing its projects, and said on 2 September 2026 that the second national data centre at Blida implements its first axis.

Last twelve months. The National Digital Services Centre was inaugurated on 5 July 2026, and the Council of Ministers of 12 July 2026 gave administrations one month to connect to the National Data Center.

Not held. No adopting act is named; approval is stated by the press and the High Commissioner only. No cost for the plan, no domestic budget line and no results against the strategy's own targets are held.

EGY.short: Egypt's Digital Egypt strategy, running from 2016, is listed as adopted in 2025, but its text, plan and recent progress are not known.
EGY.summary:
Governance and finance. The ITU repository names the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology as lead of the Digital Egypt Strategy.

Standing. The ITU repository's 2025 listing records the Digital Egypt Strategy as adopted, and on 13 March 2024 the Prime Minister named approval of a National strategy for building a fully digital state among the Supreme Council for Digital Society's objectives.

Text. The ITU repository's 2025 listing names the Digital Egypt Strategy as the country's strategy.

Period. The same repository gives its time frame as 2016 onward.

Delivery plan. At Cairo ICT'24 on 17 November 2024 the ICT minister briefed the Prime Minister on its four pillars: digital services, jobs in the digital economy, digital creativity and infrastructure.

Reporting. At the same briefing of 17 November 2024 the minister gave implementation figures, including 8 million registered on the Digital Egypt platform and 23 of a targeted 32 creativity centres built.

Last twelve months. The latest held figures are those of the 17 November 2024 briefing, when 8 million were registered on the Digital Egypt platform.

Not held. Adoption rests on a general listing with no adopting act, body or date, and no public text is held. No delivery plan, domestic budget line or reporting after November 2024 is held, and no approval of the fully digital state strategy is recorded.

ERI.short: Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy, according to a June 2026 legal-status page; whether any is in preparation is not known.
ERI.summary:
Governance and finance. Levellers, in a legal-status page reviewed on 8 June 2026, states that Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy.

Standing. The same Levellers page states that Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy, alongside no published national AI strategy.

Text. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Period. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Delivery plan. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Reporting. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Last twelve months. Levellers, reviewing on 8 June 2026, states that Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy.

Not held. The only statement of absence is a third-party legal-status page, not an Eritrean government source. No instrument in preparation is on record.

ETH.short: Ethiopia's Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030 in November 2025, but its public text and period are not known.
ETH.summary:
Governance and finance. The National Digital Transformation Council, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Temesgen Tiruneh, met on 30 July 2026 and was said to provide strategic leadership for the Digital Ethiopia Strategy. Public ICT and digital allocations rose from about USD 250 million in 2020 to USD 500 million in 2024, which Paradigm Initiative attributes to the predecessor, Digital Ethiopia 2025.

Standing. The Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030 on 29 November 2025 and the Prime Minister launched it on 20 December 2025, as the successor to Digital Ethiopia 2025.

Text. The Ethiopian News Agency describes Digital Ethiopia 2030 as a comprehensive national blueprint building on the Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda.

Period. Digital Ethiopia 2025 covered 2020 to 2025, and the Prime Minister said on 20 December 2025 that it had been completed as the country moved to Digital Ethiopia 2030.

Delivery plan. CIO Africa, on 27 January 2026, lists the targets for 2030: 100 percent 5G coverage in 100 cities, 128 million mobile subscribers, a Fayda digital ID for every adult and digital payments up sevenfold.

Reporting. On 30 July 2026 the Council reviewed progress on the Digital Ethiopia Strategy, Fayda and the 5 Million Coders initiative.

Last twelve months. Digital Ethiopia 2030 was launched on 20 December 2025, with enablers named as electricity, cybersecurity, a sovereign government cloud, broadband rollout and scaling Fayda ID and interoperable payments.

Not held. No public text is held for Digital Ethiopia 2030, and no period is stated for it. No domestic finance line is tied to the 2030 strategy, and reporting is activity only, with no published results.

GAB.short: Gabon's national digital plan covered 2020 to 2025 and has ended; a successor is not known, so no stage is set.
GAB.summary: Not held. The period of the Plan national stratégique Gabon Digital 2025 ended in 2025, and no successor is on record. A digital economy strategy was said to be in preparation in June 2025, with no act, text or period given.

GHA.short: Ghana's Digital Economy Policy and Strategy was adopted in 2024 with a 2028 target; whether any progress report exists is not known.
GHA.summary:
Governance and finance. The 2024 text of the Ghana Digital Economy Policy and Strategy names government budgetary support, development partner support and public-private partnerships as its funding sources, with no allocation or budget line.

Standing. The Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation adopted the Digital Economy Policy in October 2024, and the World Bank records the strategy and policy as approved in April 2024. A successor, the National Digital Transformation and Emerging Technology Strategy, was begun by the ministry in April 2025 and is in preparation.

Text. The policy and strategy text is public, published in 2024.

Period. The text sets a target timeline of 2028 for its objectives and a review every four years.

Delivery plan. The implementation framework lists strategic actions with assigned responsibilities, phased as quick wins within 6 months, medium term at 6 to 18 months and long term at 18 to 48 months, with no cost stated.

Reporting. The policy text assigns responsibilities for each strategic action and sets a review every four years.

Last twelve months. The latest dated event held for the policy is its adoption by the ministry in October 2024.

Not held. No progress report against the policy's own actions and no mandated body are held. The successor strategy is only begun, and no budget line is given for the policy.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2023-2027 digital strategy is public and costed, with a lead ministry named, but whether any progress report exists is not known.
GIN.summary:
Governance and finance. The Stratégie nationale de digitalisation de l'État et de développement de l'économie numérique 2023-2027 names the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy as lead ministry, and its financing table puts the State at USD 209,711 thousand, 12 percent of USD 1,747,590 thousand, with development partners at 60 percent.

Standing. The strategy, titled Guinée Digitale 2027 in its own text, is the Transition Government's strategy in version 1.2 of 11 June 2024, validated in national workshops with UNDP and the African Development Bank.

Text. The full text is published as a PDF on the site of the state digitalisation agency, issued by the ministry.

Period. The strategy is titled 2023-2027 and sets 14 result indicators against 2022 references for a 2027 horizon. It follows the 2016-2020 ICT and digital economy strategy, which has ended.

Delivery plan. The roadmap sets 245 initiatives under 41 orientations and six axes, each with a responsible body, a cost in thousand US dollars and a duration.

Reporting. The lead ministry is responsible for drafting, coordinating, implementing and evaluating the strategy, with a national steering committee to be set up.

Last twelve months. The latest dated row is a round table on 4 and 5 December 2024, where the minister said the strategy had been in implementation since 2022.

Not held. No implementation or results report is held, and no adopting act is named for the strategy. The period reads 2027 in the title and 2026 in one article.

GMB.short: The Gambia's Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 is published and reported adopted in 2024; its delivery plan and any progress report are not known.
GMB.summary:
Governance and finance. The National Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 is issued by the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy.

Standing. The Digital Cooperation Organization reports that the government adopted the master plan, with data current to September 2024. A separate National Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2028 was validated at a workshop on 16 and 17 May 2024.

Text. The plan's PDF is published on the ministry's website, with 2024 as its published year.

Period. The ministry's own document gives the plan's period as 2024 to 2034.

Delivery plan. The ministry's published plan document sets out the plan for 2024 to 2034.

Reporting. The Digital Cooperation Organization lists the master plan, 2024 to 2034, among the guidelines it consulted.

Last twelve months. An article of 7 October 2026 gives the master plan as running 2024-2034.

Not held. The master plan has no governance, delivery plan or reporting row of its own. Its adoption rests on one third-party report naming the government and September 2024, and some sources date the plan 2023-2033.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau adopted a 2025-2030 digital transformation strategy by decree in March 2025, with a public text, but any report on results is not known.
GNB.summary:
Governance and finance. UNDP's record of the Mais Digit@l programme shows a US$3,360,500 grant for 2025-2030 to implement the strategy, and its 2024 annual report says the strategy was launched with financing from the Government of Japan.

Standing. Decreto 10/2025, published in the Boletim Oficial on 28 March 2025 after Council of Ministers approval on 13 March, approves the ENTD.GW 2025-2030, which the government had launched on 29 January 2025.

Text. The full text is public as the annex to the gazetted decree.

Period. The stated period is 2025-2030.

Delivery plan. The strategy sets 55 interventions under six strategic objectives, each with a stated start, end and duration in months, and no cost is given for them.

Reporting. UNDP's 2024 annual report says the strategy has six pillars and 55 priority interventions with clear implementation milestones.

Last twelve months. UNU-EGOV reported on 23 September 2026 that a Project Document for implementing the strategy, to set priorities, define governance structures and identify partners and resources, was discussed with a ministry delegation on 9 September 2026.

Not held. No published report against the strategy's targets is held, and no cost is given for its actions. No mandated body is stated.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea's national digital economy strategy was in drafting with World Bank support in September 2026, and its adoption and published text are not known.
GNQ.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Civil Aviation, led by Minister of State Honorato Evita Oma, opened a World Bank-supported working week on 2 September 2026 to finish the strategy.

Standing. The Estrategia Nacional de Economía Digital was in drafting on 2 September 2026, when a four-day working week opened in Malabo with eight World Bank Group specialists to complete and validate it. The earlier ADIGE digital agenda was launched by the ministry in 2019 for 2019 to 2025.

Text. The government press office of 2 September 2026 describes the strategy as still to be completed and validated.

Period. On 2 September 2026 the ministry expected a consensus roadmap at the close of the working week.

Delivery plan. The World Bank-supported working week of 2 September 2026 aims to complete the strategy.

Reporting. The government press office reported the opening of the working week on 2 September 2026.

Last twelve months. The working week to finish the strategy opened on 2 September 2026, with the ministry expecting a consensus roadmap at its close.

Not held. No adopting act, period, plan or reporting is held for the strategy, and no text is published. No body or finance is stated.

KEN.short: Kenya published a costed national digital master plan for 2022-2032, but any published report against its targets is not known.
KEN.summary:
Governance and finance. The plan names the ICT Authority as the main coordinating and implementing agency, under an inter-ministerial committee and an oversight committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary (2022).

Standing. The Kenya National Digital Master Plan 2022-2032 is issued by the Ministry of ICT, Innovation and Youth Affairs with a Cabinet Secretary foreword, and was unveiled and launched by ICT Cabinet Secretary Joe Mucheru on 12 April 2022.

Text. The full plan is published as a PDF on the ICT Authority site.

Period. The plan states its period as 2022-2032 and is the successor to the 2014-2017 master plan. Its predecessor as national strategy is the Digital Economy Blueprint of 2019.

Delivery plan. Table 6.1 gives a resource requirement per theme for each year 2022-2032 in Ksh millions, and Annex 1 a budget per key project, for example Ksh 118.0B for 52,000 km of government fibre in 2022-2030.

Reporting. The ICT ministry's 2026 Budget Policy Statement, presented to the National Assembly committee on 17 February 2026, was aligned with the plan.

Last twelve months. An ICT Authority tender of 15 September 2026 cites the plan's national target of 100,000 km of fibre network.

Not held. No published report against the plan's targets is held, and no domestic budget line is stated. No dated event in the last twelve months changes the plan's standing.

LBR.short: Liberia has a National Digital Strategy 2025-2029, adopted per a March 2026 policy, with a costed plan, but results against its targets are not known.
LBR.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications developed the strategy and is responsible for implementing it, according to the National Data Governance Policy of March 2026, and the strategy's costs are to be met from government, multilateral donor and other sources.

Standing. The National Data Governance Policy of March 2026 lists the National Digital Strategy (2025-2029) among the instruments Liberia has adopted, after a validation workshop on 11 December 2024.

Text. The strategy's full text is published on the ministry's website.

Period. The strategy covers 2025 to 2029.

Delivery plan. In the text published on 3 February 2026, Chapter 6 estimates US$151.813 million over 2025-2029 from government, multilateral donor and other sources, and a separate US$776.250 million for about 1,500 cell towers through public-private partnership. Chapter 7 sets an implementation roadmap with timelines.

Reporting. The Digital Transformation Working Group, activated in October 2025, is to coordinate Liberia's digital activities.

Last twelve months. The strategy was officially launched at the National Coordination Session of Digital Liberia Week, held during 28-30 October 2025.

Not held. No progress report against the strategy's targets is held. No adopting act or date is named for the strategy, and no budget line for it is named.

LBY.short: Libya's Prime Minister approved a government digital transformation strategy in April 2025, to 2030, but its approved text is not known.
LBY.summary:
Governance and finance. Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dabaiba of the Government of National Unity approved the National Strategy for Government Digital Transformation, prepared by the Supreme Committee for Digital Transformation.

Standing. The Prime Minister approved the strategy on 21 April 2025, following the General Information Authority's December 2022 proposal.

Text. The General Information Authority publishes the December 2022 proposal for the strategy, marked as a proposal on its cover.

Period. The vision is that by the end of 2030 everyone in Libya will enjoy world-class government services, with 2030 targets set against 2022 baselines.

Delivery plan. The proposal sets 2030 targets against 2022 baselines, such as a rise in Libya's e-government development index rank from 162 to 100, and lists eleven action areas with initiatives. It says a national plan of projects and the budgets are still to be set.

Reporting. At the April 2025 launch the General Information Authority chairman said some of the strategy's plans had already been implemented in a number of ministries and bodies.

Last twelve months. On 19 April 2026 the General Information Authority described Level 3 biometric digital identity trials as part of implementing the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030, the name it also uses for the strategy.

Not held. The text of the strategy as approved in April 2025 is not held, only the December 2022 proposal. No budget, mandated body or results report is held for it.

LSO.short: Lesotho's digital transformation strategy to 2030 was approved in February 2025 and is published, but its action plan and results are not known.
LSO.summary:
Governance and finance. The National Digital Policy 2024-2035 says technical assistance from the International Telecommunication Union was used to draft the National Digital Transformation Strategy: Agenda 2030.

Standing. The finance minister told Parliament on 19 February 2025 that the Digital Transformation Strategy had been approved, without naming an approving act or body.

Text. The strategy's text is published on the government's website.

Period. The strategy is catalogued as Lesotho's national digital transformation strategy to 2030, self-dated 2024.

Delivery plan. The National Digital Policy lists development of a detailed action plan for the strategy as a task for 2024-2025.

Reporting. A government news item of 29 September 2026 says Lesotho is advancing the strategy, with priorities including connectivity, digital skills, innovation and technology for public services.

Last twelve months. On 29 July 2025 the minister said the memorandum of understanding with India was signed in the wake of the strategy's launch.

Not held. No adopting act or date is named for the strategy, and no governing body, finance or results report is held for it. Its action plan was still to be developed in 2024-2025, and no later one is held.

MAR.short: Morocco has Maroc Digital 2030, listed as adopted in 2025, with MAD 11 billion for 2024 to 2026, but a public text is not known.
MAR.summary:
Governance and finance. The ITU repository names the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform as lead of Maroc Digital 2030, and Morocco World News says MAD 11 billion was allocated for 2024-2026.

Standing. The ITU repository lists Digital Morocco 2030 among the strategies it says countries have adopted, and the Government Council heard a presentation of its general orientations on 25 January 2024. It follows Maroc Numeric 2013 and Maroc Digital 2020.

Text. We Are Tech Africa says Maroc Digital 2030 was launched in September 2024.

Period. The ITU repository gives its time frame as 2024-2030.

Delivery plan. Morocco World News pairs the MAD 11 billion for 2024-2026 with targets of 3,000 start-ups, 100,000 people trained a year and 240,000 jobs by 2030.

Reporting. In its declaration to the African Telecommunications Union conference in Abuja, Morocco highlighted progress under Maroc Digital 2030, without figures.

Last twelve months. On 17 July 2026 the ministry signed a memorandum with Capgemini Maroc on AI skills, and on 4 June 2026 one with Orange Morocco, both presented as implementing it.

Not held. No public text of Maroc Digital 2030 is held, and its adopting act and date are not stated. Results against it are not given beyond a general account of progress.

MDG.short: Madagascar has the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028, presented in 2024 with a USD 800 million estimate, but its adoption and public text are not known.
MDG.summary:
Governance and finance. UNDP says the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028 is coordinated by the digital ministry, supported by the Unité de Gouvernance Digitale attached to the Presidency, and the ministry estimates its budget at USD 800.169 million, of which USD 152.334 million is available.

Standing. Newsmada reports the digital minister presented the plan on 19 January 2024, and UNDP calls it formalised and in implementation in December 2025. A national digital roadmap is in preparation after the Digital Readiness Assessment report was handed over on 17 December 2025.

Text. 2424.mg reports the ministry delivered a national Plan stratégique du numérique 2023-2028 on 26 October 2023.

Period. UNDP names the plan as the national digital strategy for 2023-2028.
